d: Add Single-Leg Leg Press to the exercise library
det: Hugo hit this doing legs today: swapping off Leg Press had no single-leg option, even though every other major leg movement already has one (squat, leg extension, RDL, calf). Added sl_leg_press (machine, quad/glute, 10 reps/leg) — it now shows up under 'Same muscle group' in the manual swap sheet and in exercise search. Checked free-exercise-db for a demo GIF (no unilateral leg press exists there); shows the same styled placeholder + tappable video demo treatment as the library's other GIF-less exercises. Also updated the AI make_legs_unilateral tool: Leg Press now converts to Single-Leg Leg Press instead of Reverse Lunge, since a direct equivalent exists now.

d: Fix — logging or swapping a single exercise inside an extra gym session on a ride day did nothing
det: When a ride day has a stacked gym session added ("+ Add workout"), the per-exercise 'Log sets' and 'Busy' buttons inside that extra session's exercise list were wired with an undefined date, because the list was rendered from an object that only carried the exercise IDs. Log sets silently did nothing; swapping an exercise closed the picker as if it worked but never changed anything. The big 'Log workout' button at the bottom of that section was unaffected and always worked. Now the exercise list for an extra gym session carries its date and type like every other exercise list, so both buttons work per-exercise too.

d: Fix: tapping Log sets could open a different exercise — and save your sets to it
det: Reported with a screenshot: tapping Log sets on Glute Bridge (a Legs day) opened a sheet titled T-Bar Row, showing that exercise's PR and its already-logged sets. CAUSE: the day card and the set sheet disagreed about how to find an exercise. The card looks it up by ID — rExList does exercises.find(e=>e.id===id) — but openExLog was handed the ID and ignored it, reading log.exercises[planIndex] instead. Those two lists only line up while the log is a faithful copy of the plan. They drift apart as soon as the day's type is changed after logging has started (the plan becomes Legs while the log still holds the Pull exercises it was created with), the coach swaps an exercise, or the log arrives from a CSV import or an auto-logged session. Once drifted, position 1 in the plan (Glute Bridge) and position 1 in the log (T-Bar Row) are different exercises. This was not only a wrong title: exLogTog and exLogAdd write to that same index, so every set typed into the sheet was saved against the wrong exercise, and ticking one could set a PR on a lift you had not done. The same mistake sat in doExSwap, which replaced log.exercises[planIndex] when swapping — quietly destroying the logged sets of whichever exercise happened to occupy that slot. FIX: both now resolve the log entry by exercise ID, matching how the card already worked. If the tapped exercise is in the plan but missing from the log (day re-typed, or the log was created empty by an auto-logged session) it now gets a proper entry instead of the button doing nothing. Existing logs are left exactly as they are — sets recorded against the old day type are real training and stay in your history; they simply no longer sit in the way.

d: Fix — a gym workout logged on the same day as a ride no longer disappears
det: If you rode and then did a gym session on the same day, the app could make the gym workout look erased. When the ride synced, it offered to "make it a ride day" even though you had already logged sets, and accepting turned the day into a ride day — which never displayed that day's gym log, and pushed the session you'd just done onto a later day. Your sets were still saved, just hidden. Now: the app no longer offers to replace a gym day once you've logged sets on it — it treats the day as "did both" and shows the ride alongside your workout. If a day was already converted, its logged sets now appear on the ride day under "logged this day". The AI coach follows the same rule.

d: Swapping one gym day for another now rebalances the rest of your week
det: Changing a planned gym day to a different gym session — say Push to Pull — used to make the Push simply disappear: the day became Pull, any later Pull was set to Rest, and nothing else in the week picked up the Push. Now it is a real swap. If another upcoming day already has Pull, that day takes the Push instead, with a freshly generated set of exercises. If no day has Pull, the Push moves to your next Rest day. Only if there is no free day left is it skipped, and the app says so. The swap menu also previews this before you choose — for example "↔ Thu becomes Push" — so you know what the rest of your week will look like. Past days, locked days and any day with sets already logged are never changed.

d: Changing Rest to Push (etc.) auto-sets the later duplicate gym day to Rest
det: Hugo: once today's Rest becomes Push, nothing cleared the later Push — the week ended with two Push days. No new Swap UI. Rule lives in doSwap (Change-workout sheet and Ask Coach change_day_type). When you change a day TO Push/Pull/Legs/Upper Pump/Full Body, any later same-type day in that week that is not completed and not locked is set to Rest. Past days are never touched. Completed gym logs are never touched. A later day with a partial in-progress log is left alone with an amber toast instead of a confirm dialog. Toast when cleared: "Friday set to Rest — already have Push on Wednesday." Also: Gym→Rest relocation skips if that gym type is already scheduled later, so cascade cannot invent a second copy.

d: Plates mode now has a real Bar control — pick 45/35/25 lb or 20/15/10 kg
det: Hugo pointed out that plates mode only showed plate chips; the bar was hard-coded at 45 lb / 20 kg and only mentioned in hint text. Each plates set card now has a Bar −/value/+ control (first chip) that cycles the common bar options for the current unit (lbs 45→35→25, kg 20→15→10). The chosen bar is stored on the set as set.bar, platesTotal and decomposePlates use it, and empty plates alone correctly yield exactly the bar weight as set.w. Unit toggle clears plates+bar and re-decomposes from the converted set.w, same as before. Assisted machines stay number-only.

d: Set-logger weight −/+ fixed, plus optional plates-per-side entry
det: Two logging fixes. (1) WEIGHT −/+: the step buttons beside each set weight were effectively stuck on the kg step (2.5) even in lbs mode, because adjW compared the stored unit against "lb" with a "kg" default while the rest of the app uses "lbs"/"kg" (default lbs). They now step 5 lbs or 2.5 kg correctly, read the visible input first so they stay in sync after a unit toggle or mid-edit typing, and update both the main log rows and the day-modal rows. Toggling lbs↔kg also converts the saved set.w values (not just the on-screen inputs), so −/+ after a unit change no longer jumps back to the old number. (2) PLATES MODE: on the set logger you can toggle between number/step entry and plates-per-side. Plates mode lists common plates (lbs 45/35/25/10/5/2.5, kg 20/15/10/5/2.5/1.25), includes a standard bar (45 lb / 20 kg) in the running total, and writes that total into the same set.w field PRs and sync already use. Preference is remembered. Assisted-machine exercises stay on number entry only — plates do not apply to assistance weight.

d: Strength sessions now also arrive via intervals.icu — a second route in, no pairing code needed
det: v3.13 brought Vitruvian workouts in through Apple Health and the worker inbox. This adds an independent second route: if a strength session lands in intervals.icu — via the Intervals.icu Companion app mirroring Apple Health, HealthFit, a watch strength workout, or a manual FIT upload — the app now pulls it in as well. Since intervals.icu is already connected for rides, this route needs no extra setup at all. The pull is deliberately kept out of icuFetchActivities(): that one appends to the ride list, which feeds the bike fitness curve, so a gym session in there would have quietly inflated your cycling CTL. Strength sessions go to the day log instead, down the same path as the Health bridge. Both routes now share duplicate detection matched within a 15-minute window rather than on the exact instant, because the two sources clock the same workout slightly differently — an exact compare would have had them overwrite each other on every app open. The day card names which route delivered the session, and Check now drains both. The limit is unchanged and applies to both: neither Apple Health nor a FIT file carries sets, reps or weight, so the lifts themselves still come from pasting your summary into Ask Coach.

d: Vitruvian workouts now log themselves — finish on the Trainer+ and the session is already here
det: Vitruvian publishes no API, so this doesn't connect to Vitruvian at all — it rides the trail Vitruvian already leaves. Vitruvian writes each finished workout to Apple Health; a one-time iOS Shortcut automation ("When Vitruvian is closed") reads that workout and posts it to the app's Cloudflare worker, where it waits in a small inbox; the app drains that inbox every time it opens. Your phone and the app are never awake together, which is why the queue exists. Sessions land on the day they happened — on extralog_ if a ride already owns that day, matching the extra-gym convention — and are marked complete, so the layoff scan and streaks count them. Crucially a session is only cleared from the inbox once it is safely stored, because the cloud pull overwrites local days outright; anything unconfirmed is simply re-delivered next open and recognised as already logged. WHAT IT CANNOT DO: Apple Health has no field for sets, reps or weight, so those never leave the Vitruvian app. The day card says so plainly rather than staying quiet about it, and offers an "Add my sets" button that jumps to Ask Coach primed with the right date — paste your Vitruvian summary and the existing log_gym_sets tool structures the lifts onto the same day, PRs and all. Pairing is one code in Settings → Vitruvian auto-log; that code only ever unlocks the workout inbox, never Firebase or Strava. Worker v11 adds /vitruvian/session, /pending and /ack, and needs a KV namespace bound as TB_INBOX plus a TB_INGEST_TOKEN secret.

d: Proper backup and restore — your rides and weight history were never actually being saved
det: A review turned up a real gap. The app contained a full backup function and a restore function, but neither was reachable from anywhere in the app — the only button available exported gym sets to CSV. Worse, the backup itself only covered workouts, plans and PRs: your entire ride history, weight log, profile, extra gym sessions and weekly reviews were excluded, so even a "full backup" would have quietly left most of your data behind. Fixed: the backup now saves everything the app treats as your data (it uses the same definition as cloud sync, so the two can't drift apart again), and both buttons now appear under Settings → Account as "Backup & restore". Restoring asks for confirmation first, shows when the backup was taken, and ignores anything unrecognised — previously it would have written every key in the file without warning. Temporary caches are deliberately left out, so backups stay small.

d: Ready for indoor season — Apple Watch and spin-bike workouts now come through properly
det: Getting set up for winter training on a spin bike. (1) Indoor rides were at risk of being dropped entirely: the app only recognised a short list of activity names, and an Apple Watch "Indoor Cycle" (or a Peloton/spin session routed through Apple Health) can arrive under several different names depending on which app forwards it. All the common indoor and trainer names are now recognised. (2) Indoor sessions no longer show misleading empty stats — a spin-bike ride with no GPS used to display "0.0 km" and "0 m elevation"; those are now simply left out, so you see the numbers that exist (time, heart rate, and power if your bike reports it). (3) Rides are correctly labelled Indoor rather than Outdoor across all the indoor activity types. (4) Heart-rate-only indoor sessions still get a training-load estimate, so your Fitness and Form keep tracking through winter even without a power meter. Note: Apple Health has no web connection of its own — an iPhone app such as Intervals Companion or HealthFit forwards Apple Watch workouts to intervals.icu, and from there they reach this app automatically.

d: Connect your own Endurain server — plus honest wording about Strava
det: Two changes. (1) ENDURAIN: if you self-host Endurain, the app can now pull rides straight from it — no third-party service in between. Add your server address and sign in under Settings → Ride sync → Ride sources; only the access token is kept, never your password. Rides arrive with power, normalized power, heart rate, elevation and calories, and are labelled as coming from Endurain. It syncs automatically on app open like the other sources, and non-cycling activities are filtered out. Two requirements: the server must be reachable over https, and it must be configured to allow requests from this app's web address — the app explains this if the connection is refused. (2) STRAVA WORDING: the app no longer states that Strava requires a paid subscription unless Strava has actually reported that to the app. If you have not connected Strava, it simply offers to connect; the subscription explanation appears only when Strava itself returns the "inactive application" response.

d: Ride sessions now explain themselves — and tell you the watts to aim for
det: A heading like "Sweet Spot" means nothing on its own. Every ride session now carries a one-line explanation of what it is and why it's in your week, plus — if your FTP is set — the actual power range to target. For a 256W FTP, Sweet Spot reads "Aim for ~225-238W", Tempo "~195-223W", Recovery "~115-154W", and so on, so the session name turns into something you can act on. There's also an ⓘ next to the name opening a fuller explanation, including why the weeks rotate: your rides run a repeating 4-week cycle (Build 1 → Build 2 → Peak → Recovery), each week using a different session type — Tempo, Sweet Spot, Hills, then easy — so you develop different systems rather than repeating the same ride. If you haven't set an FTP, it says so instead of inventing numbers.

d: No more Strava error popping up every time you open the app
det: If Strava had deactivated the app's API access, the automatic sync on every launch failed and threw the same red error on screen each time — for a sync you never asked for, about a service you may have deliberately stopped using. Background syncs are now silent when they fail: the app skips the Strava call entirely once it knows access is deactivated, and only reports failures when you actually tap a sync button yourself. Nothing is hidden — the current state and the exact error are still in Settings → Ride sync, and "Check again" re-tests whenever you want. You can leave Strava connected indefinitely without it nagging you.

d: Ride settings tidied into one section — and rides now say where they actually came from
det: Three fixes. (1) SETTINGS were sprawling: Strava, intervals.icu and file import each had their own full-height card stacked down the page, even when two of them weren't in use. They're now a single "Ride sync" section — one compact line telling you sync is working and when it last ran, with setup, alternatives and any dead connection folded behind a "Ride sources & setup" toggle (flagged if something needs attention). (2) LABELS: rides were tagged "Strava" everywhere regardless of origin, so a ride imported from Garmin still claimed to be from Strava. Each ride now shows its real source — intervals.icu, Garmin, or Strava — on day cards, the week list, ride details and History. (3) AVERAGE POWER is now its own figure on the ride card next to Normalized Power, instead of small print underneath it. Also added glossary entries explaining Sweet Spot and the Build/Peak/Recovery week cycle.

d: Import your whole ride history from one Garmin CSV file
det: Garmin Connect's Activities page has an "Export CSV" button that downloads every activity in a single file — the app now accepts it. One file brings in your entire history at once, complete with Garmin's own Normalized Power and Training Stress Score, which are used directly rather than re-estimated. Rides are matched to the right type (road, mountain, e-MTB, gravel, indoor), non-cycling activities and aborted zero-second entries are skipped, and anything already in the app is detected and not duplicated — so you can re-import the same file safely. This is the quickest way to backfill after a break, or if you'd rather not connect anything at all. Single-ride TCX and GPX files still work for maximum detail on one session.

d: "You rode on a gym day" now asks you on the home screen — plus readable errors and the missing Disconnect button
det: Three fixes. (1) RIDE ON A GYM DAY: when a ride landed on a day planned as Push/Pull/Legs, the app offered to swap the day and push the gym session forward — but that choice only appeared once you tapped into the day, so from the home screen it looked like the ride had been ignored. The prompt now appears on the week view itself: it names the ride, says what was planned, and gives you three options — make it a ride day (cascading the gym workout forward through the week), keep both, or decide later. It hides once handled, and never appears for rest days, future days, or days where you did the gym anyway. (2) ERROR MESSAGES: long messages were set to never wrap, so they ran off both edges of the screen and were unreadable — exactly when you most needed to read them. They now wrap, stay within the screen, and stay visible longer the longer they are. (3) The Disconnect button had gone missing from the Strava card when Strava had deactivated API access, leaving no way to remove a dead connection. Restored.

d: Automatic Garmin ride sync is back — for free, via intervals.icu
det: Strava putting API access behind a subscription broke automatic ride syncing. Rather than settle for manual file imports, the app now uses intervals.icu as the bridge instead: Garmin Connect syncs your activities into intervals.icu automatically, and the app pulls from its free API on every open — exactly the hands-off flow you had before, at no cost. Setup is one-time: sign up free at intervals.icu, connect Garmin under Settings → Connections, copy your API key from Developer Settings, and paste it into Settings here. Rides arrive with distance, time, heart rate, power, cadence and elevation, plus training load and intensity calculated by intervals.icu from your full power stream — which is actually more accurate than the estimate the app derived from Strava data, so your Fitness/Fatigue/Form numbers improve. Existing rides from Strava or file imports are kept and merged, never duplicated. Strava remains supported if you ever subscribe, and file import stays as a fallback.

d: Import rides straight from a Garmin file — no Strava, no subscription needed
det: Strava now requires a paid subscription for API access, which switched off automatic ride syncing. This makes the app independent of it. In Garmin Connect, open a ride → ⚙ → Export to TCX (or GPX), then in Settings → "📁 Import a ride file" pick the file — you can select several at once. Distance, moving time, heart rate (average and max), power, cadence and elevation gain are read directly from the file, and Normalized Power is calculated properly (30-second rolling average) so training load and your fitness curve match previously synced rides exactly. Imported rides behave like any other: they appear on your day cards and in History, count toward Fitness/Fatigue/Form, and feed the AI coach. Re-importing the same ride is detected and skipped, so you cannot create duplicates. TCX carries the most data (power and heart rate); GPX works too but usually has no power.

d: Identifies the real Strava problem: Strava deactivated the app's API access
det: The diagnostics added in v3.01 revealed the actual cause of rides not syncing, and it was not what the earlier versions guessed. Strava replies: {"resource":"Application","field":"Status","code":"Inactive"} — Strava has marked the whole API application inactive, which it does when the Strava account owning the app's API key has no active Strava subscription (a Developer Program requirement). Signing in still works, which is why the app looked connected while every ride request was refused. Crucially, reconnecting can never fix this, yet v3.00/v3.01 told you to reconnect and tick a permissions box — wrong advice for this error. The app now recognises this specific response and says plainly what it is: Strava API access is deactivated, it needs a subscription on the owning account plus reactivation at strava.com/settings/api, and reconnecting will not help. Manual ride logging still works on any ride day, and nothing else in the app is affected.

d: Strava errors now show what Strava actually said, instead of just a number
det: Chasing a stubborn "activities 403", the app was throwing away the most useful information it had: Strava sends a description of what is wrong with every rejected request, and the app discarded it and displayed only the status code. Now the exact response from Strava is captured and shown in Settings → Strava, alongside the app version and a timestamp, so a failure can be diagnosed instead of guessed at. It stays on screen rather than vanishing with the toast, and clears automatically after a successful sync. Also added a "🔁 Reconnect" button to the normal connected card (previously reconnecting meant disconnecting first), and refreshed the offline cache so updates land promptly rather than a version behind.

d: Fixes the Strava "403" after authorising — the permission screen now always appears
det: Reconnecting Strava could fail with a bare "403" straight after you authorised it. Cause: the app asked Strava for approval with "auto", which tells Strava to silently reuse whatever permissions you granted it previously instead of showing the permission screen. If that earlier grant didn't include activity access — or the "View data about your activities" box was left unticked — Strava handed back a token that isn't allowed to read your rides, so every sync answered 403 with nothing explaining why. Three fixes: (1) the app now always shows Strava's permission screen when you connect, so activity access can actually be granted; (2) it reads the permissions Strava reports back and, if activity access is missing, tells you exactly which box to tick instead of saving a token that can't work; (3) a 403 or 401 from Strava now produces a plain-English message and flags the connection for reconnecting, rather than printing a status code.

d: Strava reconnect fix — a dead connection now says so instead of failing silently
det: If Strava stopped accepting the app's saved access — revoked in your Strava settings, or gone stale over a long break — the app handled it badly. It kept using the expired token, sync failed with a cryptic "activities 401", and Settings still cheerfully showed "Strava connected" with no way to fix it. Now: (1) the app recognises when Strava has rejected its access and stops retrying a dead token; (2) Settings shows a clear amber "Strava needs reconnecting" card with a one-tap Reconnect button, and reassures you that rides already synced are safe; (3) if a background sync finds the connection dead, a toast tells you — so you're not left wondering why new rides stopped appearing; (4) fixed a latent bug where a refresh response without a new refresh token would overwrite the stored one with nothing, permanently breaking every future refresh. Reconnecting never deletes ride history.

d: Comeback mode fixes — the eased return now actually ramps over both weeks
det: Four fixes found by walking through what happens when you open the app after a long break. (1) VOLUME RAMP: the comeback block reduced your training days in week 1, but week 2 jumped straight back to a full 4-5 day week — the exact volume spike a graded return exists to prevent. Week 2 now steps up by one day instead (e.g. 2 easy days → 3), then normal service resumes. (2) STALE DETECTION: the "welcome back" check ran once on the first screen draw, before Strava had finished syncing — so if you'd actually ridden during your break, the app could still greet you as detrained until you reloaded. The check now refreshes whenever new workout or Strava data arrives. (3) Extra gym sessions logged on ride days now count as training for that check (they were invisible to it). (4) Tapping "Start comeback plan" announced "plan ready" instantly, even though building the week needs your location and can fail or be declined — the message now says what it's doing rather than claiming a result it doesn't have yet.

d: New ⓘ buttons explain the training jargon — TSS, FTP, TSB and friends in plain English
det: The coach and charts use sports-science shorthand (Load/TSS, Fitness/CTL, Fatigue/ATL, Form/TSB, FTP, NP, Intensity, RPE, Zone 2, tonnage, estimated 1RM…) and nothing in the app explained them. Small ⓘ buttons now sit wherever the jargon is densest — the Ask Coach header, the day-screen coach card, the logged-ride detail card, and the Cycling Performance and Gym Progress sections in My Training. Tapping one opens a plain-English glossary of all 16 terms, scrolled to and highlighting the most relevant entry for where you tapped (e.g. the ride card jumps to Load/TSS). Each explanation is 2-3 friendly sentences with practical reference points — like "an easy hour is ~40-50 TSS" or "RPE 7 = about 3 clean reps left in the tank" — plus why assisted-machine numbers run backwards.

d: Smarter daily coaching — the AI now knows your FTP, fatigue, weather and today's targets
det: Upgrade pass on what the AI coach actually sees before giving advice. (1) RIDE NOTES: the daily pre-ride coach was asked for "specific power targets" without ever being told your FTP — targets were guesses. It now gets your FTP with computed Zone 2 / threshold power bands (or is told to use HR/RPE targets if FTP isn't set), your current fitness/fatigue/form (CTL/ATL/TSB), yesterday's ride load, the planned session and duration, today's weather, and NP/TSS per ride in your history. (2) GYM NOTES: the daily pre-workout coach now sees today's actual prescription per exercise (sets×reps×RPE and the suggested weight from your card — comeback-aware), plus your current form so it can account for ride fatigue on lifting days. Assisted machines are tagged so it never suggests adding assistance as progression. (3) NEXT-WEEK WEIGHTS: the weekly suggestion prompt now carries an explicit assisted-machine exception (progress = LESS assistance). (4) LANGUAGE: daily coach notes now come back in Traditional Chinese when the app language is 繁體中文 (previously English-only). (5) RELIABILITY: the backup AI providers (used when Gemini hits quota) had a response cap that truncated weekly reviews and coach actions — raised to cover the largest responses (requires the Cloudflare worker update).

d: My Training tab fixed up — extra gym sessions now cloud-sync, search works properly, e-bike rides show in History
det: Review pass over the My Training tab. (1) SYNC FIX (important): extra gym sessions logged on ride days (the "+ Add gym workout" feature) were never included in cloud sync — they only existed on the device that logged them, so they never appeared on your other devices and would be lost with the phone. They now sync like every other log; your next full sync uploads any existing ones. (2) SEARCH: typing in the PR search box lost keyboard focus after every single character (each keystroke re-rendered the screen and destroyed the input). Focus and cursor position are now restored — you can actually type a whole word. (3) HISTORY: e-bike (EBikeSport) and e-MTB rides showed on the week view but were missing from the History list due to an out-of-date activity-type filter; all six copies of that filter are now one shared list. (4) PERFORMANCE: the tab re-scanned ~450 days' worth of logs on every render (including per keystroke); the scan is now cached and reused until a workout changes. (5) History shows the latest 25 sessions with a "Show all" button instead of rendering six months of entries at once.

d: Comeback mode for long breaks — plus smarter load tracking for rides without power
det: Four upgrades. (1) COMEBACK MODE: if you haven't logged anything for 4+ weeks, the week view now greets you with a "Welcome back" banner offering an eased 2-week re-entry: a short-week plan (2-3 full-body days depending on how long you were away), working-weight suggestions damped to 60-80% of your pre-break PRs (assisted machines get MORE help, not less), and — crucially — every AI coach prompt now includes your layoff context, so the coach stops telling you to chase pre-break PRs and instead paces your return. A status chip shows "Comeback week 1 of 2" while active; end it early anytime. Even if you decline the banner, the coach is still told about the gap. (2) RIDES WITHOUT POWER now contribute an estimated training load (from heart rate vs your observed max, or a steady-Zone-2 assumption) instead of counting as zero — previously an HR-only ride looked like a rest day, making your Form (TSB) read artificially fresh and skewing coach advice toward "push harder". Estimated loads show with a ~ prefix. (3) STRAVA SYNC now paginates — athletes with 200+ activities in 6 months no longer silently lose older rides from the fitness curve. (4) The Ask Coach prompt now lists each exercise with the same sets/reps/RPE and suggested weight the screen shows you, instead of library defaults.

d: Training-logic review — assisted-machine weight suggestions fixed, and stale caches now clean themselves up
det: Two fixes from a logic review of the coaching and planning systems. (1) ASSISTED MACHINES: the suggested working weight (the ~weight badge on exercise cards) scaled your PR by an energy multiplier — correct for normal lifts, but backwards for assisted pull-ups/dips, where the weight is how much the machine HELPS you. On a sore/recovery day it suggested roughly half your PR assistance — i.e. the hardest setting of all on your weakest day. The multiplier now inverts for assisted exercises: less energy = more assistance. Fresh suggests slightly more help than your best-ever; sore suggests ~1.45× your PR help. (2) CACHE CLEANUP: daily AI-coach snippets, weather lookups, dismissed banners and weekly-advisor caches were written every day but never deleted, slowly filling the ~5MB local storage cap on iPhones (which would eventually block workout saves — the v2.92 storage warning would have caught it, but prevention beats warning). A sweep now runs shortly after each app start and removes cache entries older than 30 days. Your workouts, plans and reviews are never touched.

d: Hardening pass — security fix in Friends, sync race fix, storage-full warning, and a crash recovery screen
det: Four robustness fixes from a full code review. (1) SECURITY: friend names in the Friends card and pending-request list were rendered without HTML escaping — since another user controls that string, a malicious "friend" could have injected script into your session (stored XSS). Names are now escaped, and the weekly-summary numbers (streak, sessions, km) are coerced to numbers so malformed data can't crash the Settings screen. (2) SYNC: fixed a race in incremental cloud sync where a set logged while a sync was already uploading could be cleared from the pending queue without ever reaching the cloud. The sync now snapshots the queue before uploading; anything changed mid-flight is picked up by the next sync, and failures restore the queue. (3) STORAGE: if the device's local storage is full (iOS caps it ~5MB), saves used to fail silently — a logged workout could just vanish. You now get a warning toast the first time a write fails. (4) RECOVERY: if a screen hits a rendering error, instead of a permanently blank page you now get a friendly error screen with "Back to my week" and "Reload" buttons plus the error message for reporting.

d: AI coach panel now starts collapsed every time you open the app — out of the way until you want it
det: The "💬 Ask the Coach" panel sat at the top of the week view expanded by default, taking real estate even when you just opened the app to check your plan or log a set. Now every fresh app open starts with the panel collapsed to its compact header bar. Tap the header to expand it (with your conversation history intact), use it, and on the next open it's tucked away again. Previously the collapse state was sticky — once expanded it stayed expanded across opens — defeating the point. The conversation thread itself still persists in the cloud as before; only the expand/collapse UI state is per-session now.

d: Garmin helper now reads correctly for cycling computer users (not just watch users)
det: The v2.89 Garmin helper was framed around a Garmin watch — the heading used a ⌚ icon and the wording implied a wearable. Fixed: heading is now "🚴 Using a Garmin (Edge / watch)?" and the explanation describes the device-neutral path: your Garmin (Edge cycling computer, Forerunner, Fenix, etc.) syncs to Garmin Connect, which auto-forwards to Strava. Same one-time setup steps; just clearer for anyone whose Garmin is a cycling computer rather than a wrist device.

d: Garmin onboarding — a clear "how to connect your Garmin" guide in the Strava settings
det: Garmin has no direct public API for a personal app, so it connects through Strava: your Garmin auto-pushes activities to Strava, and the app reads them from there (this also covers running and any other Strava-connected app). Added an expandable "⌚ Using a Garmin? How to connect" helper in the Strava section of Settings — shown whether or not Strava is connected, so it also helps anyone whose Garmin rides aren't appearing because their Garmin isn't linked to Strava yet. Walks through the one-time Garmin Connect → Connected Apps → Strava link. No change to the existing Strava connection.

d: Fix — a ride logged on a rest day now shows its details when you tap into the day
det: Bug fix. If you logged (or Strava-synced) a ride on a day the plan marked as Rest & Mobility, the week view correctly showed it as your ride — but tapping into that day still showed only the rest/stretch plan, with no ride details. Now the day screen surfaces the logged ride (distance, time, heart rate, power, elevation, cadence, training load) under a "🚴 Logged today" heading, above the optional mobility routine. The ride detail card was extracted into a shared component so rest days and planned ride days render it identically.

d: Codebase cleanup — CSS card class consolidation and incremental cloud sync
det: Visual and performance pass. (1) Extracted a card style repeated 21x into a unified `.card` CSS class in index.html, reducing code duplication and standardizing margins, borders, and paddings across the app. (2) Implemented incremental cloud sync (saveToCloud) to upload only changed keys (via local _dirtyKeys tracking and Firebase multi-path updates) instead of uploading the entire data bundle on every sync, saving mobile battery and database bandwidth.

d: Faster launches — the app now opens instantly from cache and tells you when a new version is ready
det: Performance pass. (1) The service worker switched the app shell from network-first to stale-while-revalidate: instead of waiting on a full re-download of index.html every launch, it serves the cached copy instantly and refreshes in the background — launches feel immediate even on a slow connection. When a newer version is fetched (detected by comparing APP_VERSION), a small "✨ New version ready — Reload" toast appears so updates still land, just without blocking every open. (2) Exercise GIFs no longer re-run their Image() preload + placeholder fade on every re-render (e.g. while logging sets) — once an exercise image has loaded this session it paints straight from cache, removing redundant work and a visible flicker. (3) Removed ~2MB of unused dev preview images that were shipping in the repo. No behaviour changes to your data or plans.

d: Short-week mode — compress your plan into 1, 2, or 3 days when you can't make it to the gym as often this week
det: New ⏱️ button next to the regenerate icon (or ask the AI coach "I can only train 2 days this week"). Pick 1, 2, or 3 — the plan rebuilds: 1-2 days = full-body sessions (squat, hinge, press, pull, shoulder, core), 3 days = Push/Pull/Legs split. Training days land on the best-weather slots, the rest of the week becomes recovery. Locked days (anything you already logged) are preserved. New FULL_BODY day type with a dedicated full-body exercise template. Status indicator on the week-nav shows ⏱️ Nd when an override is active; pick Auto to revert. Per-week — next week resets to your normal profile setting.

d: Auto-skip + cascade now also reaches back into last week — trailing missed days carry into this week
det: Extends v2.83. The auto-cascade now scans BACKWARDS from last Sunday: every trailing workout day with no log gets pulled into this week. Example: you skip last Sunday's Legs and today is Monday → last Sun is marked Skipped AND this Monday becomes Legs (whatever Monday was originally gets pushed to Tuesday, etc). If you skipped both Sat and Sun, the OLDER miss lands on Monday (Sat→Mon, Sun→Tue, original Mon→Wed) — chronological catch-up. The backward scan stops at last week's first completed day so sessions you actually did are never disturbed. Trailing workouts that fall off this week are caught next week via the v2.82 catch-up signal.

d: Past days with nothing logged auto-mark as Skipped and the missed workout cascades forward through the rest of the week
det: When a day passes with no completed workout (no gym sets, no Strava ride, no manual ride log), it now auto-converts to a Skipped day and its planned workout shifts into the next available day, pushing later workouts forward by one. Example: planned Tue=Push / Wed=Legs / Thu=Pull, you skip Tue, and today is Wed → Tue=Skipped, Wed=Push, Thu=Legs, Fri=Pull. Cascade stops at any already-completed day (so logged sessions are never disturbed). New SKIPPED day type added to WI map with its own grey colour and "Skipped" label. Runs idempotently on every week-view render so the layout always reflects reality. Only operates on the current week (never on past or future weeks).

d: Generate plan now directly prioritises what you skipped last week — not just inferred from gaps
det: Made the catch-up logic in getMostNeededGymType() much more direct. Before: it looked at the LAST 14 days of completed logs and prioritised whichever muscle group had the biggest gap — indirect. Now: it FIRST checks what was planned in the last 7 days but had no log, and anchors the new week's rotation on the EARLIEST of those direct misses (so the most overdue catch-up comes Monday, with any later misses falling in next). Falls back to the longest-gap logic only if there were no planned-but-skipped sessions. Practical effect: if you planned Legs on Saturday and skipped it, Monday's first gym day this week is Legs — guaranteed, not inferred. The banner from v2.81 still appears showing what was caught up.

d: Made the missed-workouts catch-up VISIBLE — banner on the week view shows what you missed and how the plan adjusted
det: The catch-up logic (since v2.64) silently prioritised muscle groups you skipped — but you couldn't tell it was working. Now an amber banner appears at the top of the week view when last week had misses: "Last week you missed Legs + 1 ride. This week starts with Legs to catch up." Dismissible (x), per-week, and re-appears after every Regenerate so you can confirm the new plan accounted for what you skipped. Only shows on the current/future week, never historical. The banner reads the prior week's plan, compares it to actual gym logs and Strava rides, and only fires when there's a real miss — so it stays out of the way when you're on track.

d: Gym-equipment preference now carries into the AI coach — it won't suggest or swap to exercises your gym lacks
det: Completing the gym-equipment work: the Ask Coach now respects your selected gym. (1) The AI prompt has a new "GYM EQUIPMENT (hard constraint)" section listing your gym name and available equipment, with explicit instructions to only suggest/swap exercises that equipment supports and to offer the closest available alternative if you ask for something the gym can't do. (2) The swap_exercise tool now rejects swapping into an exercise your gym lacks ("Your gym doesn't have the equipment for X"). (3) make_legs_unilateral skips any single-leg conversion whose variant needs equipment your gym doesn't have (keeps the original, notes how many were kept). The plan-mutating tools that generate fresh exercises (change_day_type, add_workout_to_ride_day, swap_workout_days, regenerate) already route through genSession, which has always filtered by gym equipment. So the gym preference now governs the entire app: generation, manual swap, AND the AI coach.

d: Gym-equipment filtering completed — Swap menu now respects your gym, and all exercises are equipment-tagged
det: The gym-equipment feature was already live for plan GENERATION (pick a gym → the generator only picks exercises that gym has equipment for, via filterSlot/exAvail/getActiveEquip). But two gaps remained: (1) The manual "🔄 Swap" menu showed ALL same-group alternatives regardless of your gym — so you could swap into an exercise your gym doesn't have. Now the swap suggestions (movement slot, muscle group, related) are filtered to only show exercises your selected gym supports, with a safety fallback to the full list if filtering would leave a section empty. (2) The 6 single-leg variants added in v2.68 had no equipment tags, so they bypassed the filter entirely (untagged = always shown). Tagged them now: single-leg squat/reverse lunge/single-leg deadlift/single-leg calf → dumbbell, single-leg leg extension → machine, cable kickback → cable. So picking a gym now correctly governs both generation AND swapping, across every exercise. (Note: the full-text search box in the swap sheet still searches all exercises, so you can always pick something manually if you know your gym has it.)

d: Assisted-machine logic verified across the whole app — every PR/progression/label path now respects "lower = stronger"
det: Followed up on v2.76 to make sure the assisted-exercise inversion is applied EVERYWHERE, not just the two main spots. Audited all five PR-write paths: checkPR (manual logging) ✓ and the AI log_gym_sets tool ✓ were already inverted in v2.76; CSV import and manual edit/delete take values as-is (no comparison, correct). Fixed one remaining spot: the AI weekly-review data builder was picking the "best set" by highest weight×reps and labelling "[NEW PR]" by highest weight — backwards for assisted exercises. Now for assisted machines it picks the lowest-assist set as best and labels a PR when assist is at/below your record (with "assist" noted). The whole system is driven by the EX.assist flag, so it's centralized — the two assisted machines (Assisted Pull-Up, Assisted Dip) are the only ones in the library and both are flagged; any future assisted exercise just needs the flag and every path handles it automatically.

d: "Complete Workout" now returns you to the main week view (was landing on the day-detail screen — felt like a dead end)
det: After logging a session, tapping "✓ Complete Workout" navigated to the day-detail screen instead of the main plan page, so it felt like the button didn't bounce you out. Now it returns straight to the week view with a back-slide animation, clears the active log session, and shows a "✓ Workout logged" confirmation toast. One tap = done and home.

d: Assisted exercises (pull-up/dip) now tracked correctly — weight is ASSISTANCE, so lower = stronger
det: On an assisted pull-up/dip machine, the weight you set is how much the machine HELPS you (counterweight) — so MORE weight = MORE help = easier, and getting stronger means REDUCING it toward unassisted. The app was treating it like a normal exercise (higher = better), so it celebrated "70lb assist" as a PR (it's actually the most help = weakest) and the progression target told you to ADD assistance. Fixed: (1) assisted_pull-up and assisted_dip flagged with assist:true. (2) PR logic inverted for them — a personal best is now LOWER assist weight (at equal/more reps), or same assist with more reps. So as you reduce the help, you set real PRs. (3) Progression target inverted — when you hit the top of the rep range it now suggests LESS assistance ("↓ −5lb assist"), and at 0 it prompts "try it unassisted!". (4) A clear amber note appears on assisted exercises in the log: "⚖️ This is assistance weight — lower = stronger." The weight column header shows "assist lbs". (5) The AI coach is told these are assisted so its advice points the right way. Your existing 70lb PR will be replaced automatically the next time you log a lower-assist set (or edit it manually).

d: Fix sync PERMISSION_DENIED — cloud save now uses update() instead of set(), respecting the new security rules
det: After locking down the Firebase security rules, auto-sync started failing with PERMISSION_DENIED. Root cause: saveToCloud did .set({data,updated}) on the whole users/{uid} node, which requires write permission on the entire node — but the new rules (correctly) only grant write on the data and updated CHILD paths, not the parent (so friends can write a friend-request to your sub-node without being able to overwrite your whole record). Changed .set() to .update() — it writes only the data and updated children, which the rules allow. Bonus: this also fixes a latent bug where the full set() would have wiped your profile/friends/friendRequests/advisor sub-nodes on every sync (those siblings are now preserved). No Firebase rule change needed — the rules you already pasted support this.

d: Landscape mode fixes — login/onboarding no longer clips, content clears the notch, safe-area handling on all edges
det: The app is portrait-first, but landscape was genuinely broken in places. Fixes: (1) The lock/login/onboarding screen used centered flex layout with no scroll — in landscape's short viewport, content taller than the screen got clipped at top and bottom with no way to reach it. Added overflow-y:auto and justify-content:safe center so it centers when it fits and scrolls from the top when it doesn't. (2) Added left/right safe-area insets (--sl/--sr) — previously only top/bottom were handled, so in landscape on notched phones content could hide under the notch. Now the main screen, the bottom nav, and the lock screen all pad away from the notch on whichever side it's on. The main content already centered in a 430px column so it reads fine in landscape — just now without clipping or notch intrusion. Note: this app is designed for portrait (one-handed logging at the gym); landscape is now usable but not a dedicated wide layout.

d: Ask Coach can now control individual exercises, reps, and weights — not just whole days
det: Two new tools give the AI coach full control over the contents of a gym day. (1) swap_exercise(date, from, to) — replace a specific exercise with another, e.g. "swap my barbell bench for dumbbell press on Tuesday" or "change leg extensions to hack squats today." Both names are fuzzy-matched against the library, the slot position is preserved, and any in-progress log is updated. (2) set_exercise_targets(date, exercise, sets, reps, weight) — prescribe the loading for a specific lift, e.g. "set my squat to 5 sets of 5 at 100kg on Friday" or "make today's bench 4x8." Omitted fields keep their current value; the targets pre-fill in your log so you just confirm your actual sets. To support this, the AI now sees the full exercise list (with prescribed sets×reps) for every gym day in its context — so it can reference and modify exercises by name. Both tools show a confirmation card before applying, like every other plan change. Combined with the existing day-level tools (swap days, rest, cascade) and make_legs_unilateral, the coach can now reshape your week from the calendar down to the individual set.

d: "Busy?" button renamed to "Swap" — covers any reason for switching an exercise, not just a busy machine
det: The exercise-swap button said "🔁 Busy?", implying the only reason to switch was a taken machine. But you might want a different exercise for any reason — injury, equipment missing, preference, or just variety. Renamed to "🔄 Swap" (English) / "更換動作" (Chinese). Also updated the hardcoded "Machine busy? Swap exercise" button in the set-logging view to just "🔄 Swap exercise". Same swap menu behind it — just clearer, more universal wording.

d: In-app video player — exercise demos now play inside the app (YouTube embed), no need to leave for another app
det: Tapping 📺 Tutorial (or a placeholder card) now opens an in-app sheet that plays the demo video right there in an embedded YouTube player — no app switching. How it works: the app asks the worker to find the best embeddable tutorial video for the exercise (via the YouTube Data API), caches the video ID per exercise (searched once, then free forever), and plays it inline in an iframe (works in the installed PWA, including inline playback on iOS). If the video ID isn't cached and the worker/key isn't available yet, it gracefully falls back to the old YouTube search links — so nothing breaks during setup. A "Browse more" button under the player drops to the search links if the auto-picked video isn't the right one. REQUIRES a one-time setup: a free YouTube Data API key added to the Cloudflare worker (the worker.js change is included). Until that key is live, the player falls back to search links. New yt_cache storage key (synced) holds the resolved video IDs.

d: Placeholder exercises (no GIF) are now tappable "▶ Watch demo" cards opening a video tutorial
det: For the handful of exercises with no demo GIF in the free databases (burpee, pike push-up, wall sit, foot-mobility moves), the placeholder card now shows a "▶ Watch demo" pill and is tappable — opening the YouTube tutorial search directly. Previously the placeholder looked static even though a demo was available via the separate 📺 Tutorial button. Same treatment applied to the onerror fallback, so if ANY GIF link ever breaks in future, the user still gets a clear tappable path to a video demo instead of a dead-looking card. Context: I exhausted the free hotlinkable GIF sources (free-exercise-db, wger, Wikimedia, everkinetic) — none carry these specific exercises. The only way to embed real animated GIFs for them is ExerciseDB via RapidAPI (needs an API key + a worker proxy endpoint + caching), which is a worthwhile future project when scaling but adds an external dependency. For now every exercise has either a real GIF or a tappable video demo — nobody is left without guidance.

d: Full GIF audit — every exercise checked, 7 placeholder exercises now have real demo GIFs
det: Audited all ~90 exercises in the library against the image CDNs. Every existing free-exercise-db path resolves (200), every wger.de image URL resolves (200) — no broken links. Filled in real GIFs for 7 exercises that previously showed only a coloured placeholder: Assisted Dip (→ dip machine), Assisted Pull-Up (→ band-assisted pull-up), Adductor Machine, Abductor Machine, Single-Leg Calf Raise, Side Plank (→ side bridge), and Nordic Curl (→ natural glute-ham raise). 8 exercises remain as styled placeholders because no demo image exists in any free database: Burpee, Pike Push-Up, Wall Sit, and 5 foot-mobility physio exercises (short foot, towel scrunches, arch raise, toe spread, heel raise). These show a clean labelled card (exercise name + muscle group + icon) rather than a blank box. Note: the image loader already has an onerror fallback — if any GIF link ever breaks in future, it auto-swaps to the styled placeholder, so no exercise ever shows an empty image.

d: Single-leg exercise variants + AI "make my legs single-leg" tool. Verified all leg GIFs work.
det: GIF AUDIT: checked every leg exercise image against the free-exercise-db CDN — all resolve (200). The few with no image (Nordic curl, single-leg calf, wall sit) intentionally show styled placeholders. YouTube tutorial links are dynamic search queries (exercise name + channel), so they can't break. NEW SINGLE-LEG VARIANTS added to the library: Single-Leg Squat, Reverse Lunge, Single-Leg Leg Extension, Single-Leg Deadlift, Cable Glute Kickback, Single-Leg Seated Calf — all with working GIFs, joining the existing Bulgarian Split Squat, walking lunge, step-up, single-leg glute bridge, single-leg calf, and donkey kick. They appear automatically in the manual "🔄 Swap exercise" menu under "Same muscle group" — but are NOT forced into the default rotation (no preference toggle, as requested). NEW AI TOOL: ask the coach "change my leg day to single-leg" (or "make my legs unilateral") and it calls make_legs_unilateral(date), which swaps each bilateral leg exercise to its single-leg equivalent — squat→single-leg squat, leg press→reverse lunge, RDL/curl→single-leg deadlift, hip thrust→cable kickback, leg extension→single-leg extension, calf→single-leg calf. Shows a confirmation card before applying like all plan changes.

d: Fix: chat ↑Top / ↓Latest buttons were the same purple as sent messages — now high-contrast dark
det: The floating scroll buttons in the Ask Coach thread used the accent purple (rgba(124,58,237,.92)), identical to the user's sent-message bubbles. When a button overlapped a sent bubble it was nearly invisible. Changed to a high-contrast dark pill (near-black rgba(17,24,39,.92)) with a subtle white border and stronger shadow — stands out clearly against both the purple user bubbles and the grey coach bubbles.

d: Progressive overload targets — each exercise now prescribes a weight × reps to chase, derived from your last session + goal
det: The generator was prefilling each set by simply copying your last session's numbers — no progression. Now it computes a real target using standard double-progression: (1) finds your heaviest top set from the last completed session of that exercise; (2) if every set hit the top of your goal's rep range, it bumps the weight by your goal's progression step (2.5kg/5lb for muscle/fitness/endurance, 0 for lose_weight = hold weights in a deficit) and resets to the bottom of the rep range; (3) otherwise it holds the weight and asks for one more rep. The set inputs pre-fill with the target, and a "🎯 Target: 100lb × 8" banner appears on each exercise with a coloured pill showing the move (↑ +5lb / +1 rep / hold) and a one-line reason ("hit top of 6-12 rep range — progressing weight"). No history yet? It anchors to your PR, or asks you to enter a starting weight. The rep range comes from your blended goal profile (v2.59), so muscle goals target 6-12, endurance targets 5-8, etc.

d: Removed the v2.64 "Legs skipped" banner — catch-up logic stays, the noise goes
det: The v2.64 banner used Legs as the explicit example in the wording, which made it sound like the app was hardcoded to prioritise Legs specifically. That wasn't the intent — Legs was just the example case in the original request. The catch-up LOGIC (getMostNeededGymType anchors the next week's rotation from whichever muscle group has the longest gap) is correct and stays exactly as shipped in v2.64. Just removed the visible banner that was overcommunicating. The plan quietly does the right thing without explaining itself every week. Also removed the now-unused getGymBalanceHint() helper. If you want to see why the plan looks the way it does, the Ask Coach can explain on demand.

d: Skipped muscle groups now prioritised in next week's plan — catch-up logic + visible hint banner
det: BEFORE: the planner continued the PPL rotation from whatever you last completed. If you did Pull Wed then Push Fri, next week would start at Pull again (since Push was most recent), repeating Pull while Legs got skipped for a second week. AFTER: planner now calls getMostNeededGymType() which tracks each gym type's last-completed date over a 14-day window and starts the next week's rotation from whichever type has the LONGEST gap. If Legs was skipped, Legs now leads off the next week regardless of what you did most recently. Ties (e.g. both Legs and Upper untouched) break in canonical PPL order. When all four types are hit recently, falls back to the previous behavior (oldest-first). A new 💡 hint banner appears on the Week view explaining the catch-up: "Legs skipped recently — your plan this week starts with legs so you don't fall further behind (quads, hamstrings, glutes)." Auto-hides when the plan is balanced.

d: Chat thread auto-scrolls to latest on expand + new floating ↑Top / ↓Latest navigation buttons
det: Three improvements to the Ask Coach thread. (1) AUTO-SCROLL ON EXPAND — when you tap to expand the collapsed chat panel, the thread now jumps to the very bottom so the latest message is visible immediately (in addition to the existing page-scroll that brings the panel into view). No more "where did the response go?" moments. (2) ↑ TOP BUTTON — a small floating purple pill in the top-right corner of the chat thread. Tap to smooth-scroll the thread to the very first message. Auto-hides when you're already at the top. (3) ↓ LATEST BUTTON — same pill in the bottom-right corner. Tap to smooth-scroll back to the most recent message. Auto-hides when you're at the bottom. Both buttons appear only when the thread is tall enough to scroll. Behavior follows the user's explicit request: at the top, only ↓ Latest is shown; at the bottom (default), only ↑ Top is shown; in the middle, both are visible.

d: Ask Coach collapse: tap anywhere on the header to toggle (matches exercise-card pattern)
det: v2.60 added a small ▲ button as the only way to collapse the Ask Coach panel — inconsistent with the rest of the app where exercise cards toggle on the whole header click. Updated to match: the title + tier badge + chevron on the LEFT side of the expanded header is one large click target that toggles. Right-side controls (quota counter, 🗑 Reset) stay non-collapsing. Collapsed view already had the whole-row click pattern from v2.60 — kept that, just changed the chevron from "▼ Expand" to a simpler ▶ that mirrors how collapsed exercise cards work.

d: Fix: "Set goal" weight now uses the same bottom-sheet modal as Log weight (was a leftover browser prompt)
det: There were two definitions of editWeightGoal() in the file: a clean wrapper that called openWeightSheet('goal') at line 6852, and an old browser-prompt version at line 7387 that was overriding it (later definition wins in JavaScript). When you tapped 🎯 Set goal you got the old prompt() dialog instead of the new modal. Removed the duplicate. The goal flow now uses the same bottom-sheet design as logging a weigh-in: numeric input, lb/kg toggle, live conversion, Save/Cancel/Clear buttons. Consistent with the rest of the weight UI.

d: Collapsible Ask Coach panel + auto-scroll to bottom of chat after each response
det: Two small UX improvements. (1) Collapse — the Ask Coach panel can now be collapsed to a single-row header bar when you're not actively chatting. Tap the ▲ button in the header to collapse, or tap the collapsed bar to expand again. Collapsed state shows "💬 Ask the Coach · N messages" with a "▼ Expand" hint. Preference persists across reloads via localStorage (not synced — it's a personal UI choice). Reclaims ~400px of vertical space on the Plan view when you don't need the chat. (2) Auto-scroll on response — after the coach replies, the page now scrolls so the input box is brought into view at the bottom of the viewport. This means the latest message is always visible without having to manually scroll back up. The chat thread's internal scroll also jumps to the latest message. Combined: you can scroll anywhere on the page, send a question, and when the response arrives you're back at the chat reading the answer.

d: Goal-driven plan generation — workouts shaped by your actual goals (with priority ranking) instead of random picks
det: Foundational redesign of how plans get generated. Each goal in your profile now has a structured profile defining how it should shape your week: gym/cardio ratio, rep range, RPE range, target sets per muscle group per week, exercise bias (compound/functional/balanced), and cardio focus (easy/mixed/periodised). Muscle: 70% gym, 6-12 reps, RPE 7-9, compound-first, easy cardio for recovery. Lose weight: 50/50, 8-12 reps, compounds to preserve muscle, mixed cardio, weights held in deficit. Fitness: balanced. Endurance: 30% gym/70% cardio, 5-8 reps for strength maintenance. Performance: periodised. The week generator now uses these profiles instead of looking at only your first goal: cardio_ratio determines ride count, exercise_bias determines which slot candidates get preferred (compound vs balanced). Multi-goal users get a BLENDED profile (equal weights by default — e.g. muscle + endurance averages to ~50/50 gym/cardio, 5-10 reps). NEW priority ranking: in goals setup, if you select 2+ goals, a "Priority" section appears with an EQUAL/RANKED toggle. RANKED lets you reorder with ↑↓ arrows — top = highest priority, weighted more in the blend. Default stays EQUAL. The "My Training" tab's Your Goals card now shows your actual training mix derived from your goals ("70% gym · 30% cardio · 6-12 reps · RPE 7-9 · ~14 sets/muscle/wk") so you can see exactly what your goals translate to. v2.60 will add progressive overload targets (weight × reps prescribed per set based on PRs).

d: Coach uses feeling-words instead of raw Form numbers — "carrying fatigue" not "Form of -17"
det: v2.49/v2.54 fixed the acronym problem ("Form" not "TSB") but the raw number itself is still abstract for non-cycling users. "Form of -17" tells you nothing if you don't already know the scale. Updated the prompt to add explicit DESCRIPTIVE LANGUAGE rules: the AI must translate Form numbers into feeling-words using the interpretation bands ("fully fresh", "well-rested and recovered", "productive training zone", "carrying noticeable fatigue", "deep fatigue"). The raw Form/Fitness/Fatigue numbers are now forbidden unless the user explicitly asks for them. Per-ride numbers (load, intensity, power, HR) are still allowed since they're concrete. Examples: ✓ "You're carrying noticeable fatigue from two ride days in a row" / ✗ "Your Form is -17, so…"

d: Admin tier bypasses the 4-second client throttle — truly unlimited Ask Coach usage
det: Admin is now exempt from the 4-second client-side throttle introduced in v2.56. Non-admin users (pro, basic) still get the 4-second cooldown between sends to avoid tripping Gemini's 15 RPM limit. Admin is still bounded by Gemini's API-side limits (15 RPM, 1500 RPD on free tier) and will see a friendly 429 message if they hit them — but the app no longer pre-throttles admin requests. Suitable for solo use where no one else is sharing the API key.

d: Friendlier rate-limit error message + client-side throttle to avoid tripping Gemini's 15 RPM limit
det: When you sent a few back-to-back coach messages, Gemini returned HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) and the app just showed "API 429" — opaque. Now: (1) Status code 429 shows "Too many requests in a short time. Wait ~30 seconds and try again — the free Gemini tier allows 15 requests per minute." Other known status codes also get friendly messages (403 = "API access denied", 5xx = "Gemini service is having a moment"). (2) Added a 4-second client-side throttle between Ask Coach sends. If you hit Send within 4 seconds of the last one, you get a toast "Hold on 3s — pacing requests" and the request is dropped instead of being sent. 4s = ~15/min ceiling matches the free tier so you can't accidentally trip the limit through rapid use. The throttle resets after the cooldown so genuine multi-turn conversation still flows fine.

d: Cascade no longer silently drops a workout when changing a gym day to REST + AI prefers swap over destructive change
det: Two bugs cascaded in v2.54 user-reported scenario: AI said "move Pull to Friday" but called change_day_type(Wed, REST) instead of swap_workout_days(Wed, Fri); then doSwap's cascade shifted Pull→Thu, Push→Sun, and dropped Legs off the end. Result: a week with no Push day, AI's words didn't match the action. FIX 1: doSwap is now smart. When changing a gym day to REST, it first looks for any future REST day in the week and places the displaced workout there (non-destructive — no other workouts move or get dropped). Only if NO future REST day exists does it fall back to the cascade-and-drop behavior, and the toast now explicitly warns which workout type was dropped ("Cascaded forward — Push dropped"). FIX 2: tool-selection guidance in the prompt is much more explicit — when the user wants to MOVE a workout to a specific day, the AI must use swap_workout_days (non-destructive). change_day_type(X, REST) is reserved for "just take this day off" without a target. The prompt also requires the AI's text to match the tool — saying "moving to Friday" must call swap_workout_days, not change_day_type.

d: Coach stops writing "(TSB)" alongside "Form" + becomes proactive with tool calls (no more 3-turn back-and-forth)
det: TWO fixes. (1) ACRONYM STRIPPING — the v2.49 prompt had said "use plain term first + acronym in parens" but the model interpreted that as "always write Form (TSB)". Tightened the rule: NEVER write the acronym at all. Only "Form is -17", never "Form (TSB) is -17" or "TSB -17". Added a post-processor safety net that strips parenthetical acronyms and replaces any remaining standalone TSB/CTL/ATL/TSS/IF tokens with their plain-English equivalents — even if the model slips up, the user never sees a raw acronym. (2) PROACTIVE TOOL CALLS — when you said "I'm tired, will resting today impact my week?" the model gave advice without calling change_day_type, then "Ok adjust my plan" still didn't call it (just described intent), and only "Ok" triggered the actual tool call. Three turns for one decision. Updated prompt: explicit examples that tool calls are PROPOSALS (the confirmation card is where consent happens, not a separate turn). The model should call the tool in the same response as the question, not describe what it would do and wait. Forbidden phrases like "I can adjust your plan to…" or "I will move your workout…" are flagged in the rules.

d: Hotfix — syntax error in v2.52 broke the app (escaped quotes inside a template-literal expression)
det: The v2.52 edit to the "+ Add workout" button used \" to escape double quotes inside a ${...} expression within a template literal. That works for escape sequences BETWEEN expressions in a template literal, but inside an expression in ${...} you're in normal JS land and \" is a syntax error. Result: the entire script failed to parse, app wouldn't open. Rewrote the button using a self-invoking arrow function with backtick template literals for the strings — no escaping needed, no nested-quote problems. App opens again.

d: Guest sees ALL features now — locked-but-visible state with "Sign in to unlock" CTAs instead of hiding things
det: Previous behaviour hid Ask the Coach, Friends, the "+ Add workout" button, and showed only a generic Strava-connect prompt for guests. Now every feature is visible to guests so they can see the full scope of what they'd get if they signed up. Each gated feature shows a small "🔒 SIGN IN" pill badge in its header plus a brief description of what the feature does, and a "🔓 Sign in to unlock" CTA. Specifically: (1) ASK THE COACH — guest sees the panel with disabled-look suggestion chips and a description of the AI coach, plus the unlock button. (2) FRIENDS — same pattern, with the description of what Friends does. (3) STRAVA CONNECT in Settings — explains what it does but the button now reads "🔓 Sign in to connect Strava" for guests. (4) "+ ADD WORKOUT" button on ride days — still visible but the label includes "🔒 sign in" and tapping shows a toast. Workout-log save buttons were already showing for guests with a toast on save (no change needed). Cleaner discovery — guests can see everything the app offers, not just whatever wasn't gated.

d: Welcome sheet + sample data for guests + setup tour for new users + "View intro again" button in Settings
det: Guests were getting dropped onto an empty Week view with zero explanation of what the app does. Now: (1) When you tap "Continue as Guest" on the lock screen, a proper welcome sheet appears with 6 feature cards explaining smart weekly plan, Strava sync, gym tracking, body metrics, AI Coach, and progress charts. Three CTAs at the bottom: "🎯 Try with sample data" (loads realistic mock data into the guest store — 12 Strava rides over 30 days with computed fitness curve, 5 gym logs, weight log with 4-week loss trend, FTP 230W, body weight 78.5kg with 74kg goal, 5 PRs on compound lifts), "Start fresh — empty", or "Sign up instead". The sample data lets a guest poke around every feature in action without setting anything up. (2) New signed-in users who finish goals setup now see the same welcome sheet with a "🚀 NEXT STEPS" checklist (generate plan, connect Strava, log first workout, check My Training). Only shown once — tracked via welcome_seen flag. (3) New "📖 About the app" section in Settings has a "🧠 View intro again" button so anyone can reopen the welcome anytime.

d: Plain-English everywhere: "Load" not "TSS", "Intensity" not "IF", "Fitness − Fatigue" not "CTL−ATL" + info sheet explaining all the cycling metrics
det: Sweep through every UI label that was using TrainingPeaks acronyms and replaced with plain English. Ride card badge: "📊 TSS 95 · IF 0.85" → "📊 Load 95 · Intensity 0.85". Fitness · Fatigue · Form panel: "CTL−ATL" subtitle under Form → "Fitness − Fatigue". Cycling Progress chart metric chips: "EF" → "Efficiency", "TSS" → "Load" (full label "Training Load per Ride"). Weekly Summary table column: "TSS" → "Load". History row Strava entries: "TSS X · IF Y" → "Load X · Intensity Y". NEW ⓘ button on the Fitness · Fatigue · Form section header opens an info sheet that explains each metric in plain English with concrete examples and your CURRENT NUMBERS plugged in — so you can see "Fatigue: 25" and read what that means alongside "Form: -17 = carrying fatigue, monitor recovery". Each metric chip in the chart also has a one-line hint shown below the metric label.

d: Coach uses plain-English labels — "Form" not "TSB", "Fitness" not "CTL", etc.
det: The Ask Coach prompt was letting the AI sprinkle raw acronyms (TSB, CTL, ATL, NP, IF, EF, TSS) into responses without explanation, which is confusing if you haven't memorized the cycling-coach lexicon. Updated the prompt with an explicit VOCABULARY section: CTL → "Fitness", ATL → "Fatigue", TSB → "Form", TSS → "training load", NP → "normalized power", IF → "intensity", EF → "aerobic efficiency". When the AI does need to be precise, it puts the plain term first and the acronym in parentheses ("Your Form (TSB) is -17"). No more bare "-17 TSB" mystery numbers. Existing conversation history isn't retroactively translated, but new questions get the friendlier vocabulary.

d: Ask Coach is now multi-turn — full conversation with memory, scrollable thread, follow-up questions just work
det: Single-shot Q&A replaced with a real chat thread. Each user message and coach response appears as a bubble (user right-aligned in purple, coach left-aligned in grey) inside a scrollable container. The full conversation history is sent to Gemini on every new question — so follow-ups like "what about Wednesday too?" or "actually undo that" work naturally because the model sees the previous turns. Confirmation cards for plan changes still appear inside the corresponding coach bubble, and applied actions stay visible in the thread so you can scroll back and see what got executed. A new "🗑 Reset" button at the top of the panel clears the conversation when you want a fresh start. Conversation persists across page reloads via ai_chat_session (synced through Firebase). When the AI sees applied actions from earlier in the conversation, those are summarized in its system context for the next turn so it doesn't re-propose the same change. Loading state now shows a typing-dots bubble inside the thread instead of just disabling the input. Suggested-question chips only appear when the conversation is empty (don't clutter mid-thread).

d: Ask Coach gains four more tools: mark_day_complete, set_lock_day, log_gym_sets, regenerate_remaining_week
det: Builds on v2.46's tool-calling. Four new tools the AI can call (still gated by confirmation cards before any change applies): (1) mark_day_complete(date, completed?) — flip the completion flag for a gym day. Use when user says "I finished my workout today" without dictating sets. (2) set_lock_day(date, locked?) — lock/unlock a day so future regens preserve or don't preserve it. (3) log_gym_sets(date, exercises[]) — log structured gym data. Each exercise has a name (fuzzy-matched against the library — "bench" → Barbell Bench Press) and an array of {weight, reps} sets. Updates PRs automatically. User can say "log my Push: bench 100 lb 3x8, OHP 65 lb 3x10" and the AI structures it. Returns a note about any names that couldn't be matched. (4) regenerate_remaining_week(from_date) — regenerates the plan from a date forward. Days before from_date are temp-locked so buildWeek preserves them; original lock state is restored after. Used when user wants a fresh plan for the rest of the week without losing what they've already done.

d: Ask Coach can now actually modify your plan via Gemini function calling — confirmation card before every change
det: The chatbot is no longer read-only. Four new tools the AI can call when you ask for a plan change: (1) swap_workout_days(date1, date2) — swaps types and exercises between two days; (2) change_day_type(date, new_type) — change a day to REST or any other type, with auto-cascade when a gym day becomes REST; (3) add_workout_to_ride_day(date, gym_type) — stack a gym session on top of a ride day with cascade; (4) replace_gym_with_ride(date) — convert a planned gym day to a ride day (requires a Strava ride on that date). Safety pattern: when the AI calls a tool, the response shows your normal coach text answer PLUS a purple "⚡ Proposed change" confirmation card describing exactly what will happen (e.g. "Swap Tue 26 (Pull) ↔ Wed 27 (Legs)"). You tap ✓ Apply or Skip — nothing changes until you confirm. After applying, a green "✓ done" line replaces the card so you can see what was executed. Multiple tools can be returned in one response and confirmed independently. The AI is instructed to only call tools when you explicitly ask for changes (questions like "am I overtraining?" still get pure text answers).

d: Ask Coach sees full week plan + knows its capabilities (read-only for now, points users to UI buttons for changes)
det: Two small but important upgrades to the v2.44 Ask Coach prompt. (1) The AI now receives the FULL current week plan (all 7 days, with type, lock state, completion status, and any extraGym additions) — not just today's plan. So if you ask "swap my Tuesday Pull to Wednesday," the AI can actually see what's on Wednesday and reason about whether the swap makes sense. (2) The prompt now explicitly tells the AI what it CAN do (analyse, suggest, recommend) vs CANNOT do (directly modify plan, log workouts, swap days). When the AI recommends a change, it now points the user to the specific UI button to tap — "Swap ↕" on the week row, "+ Add workout" on a ride day, or "🔄 Replace gym with ride" prompt when Strava logs a ride on a gym day. No more false promises like "I'll swap them for you." Full plan-modification via Gemini function calling is the bigger v2.46 work — that'll let the AI actually execute the change (with a confirmation card before applying).

d: Ask the Coach — interactive AI Q&A on the Week view, with tiered access (admin/pro/basic) to cap API costs
det: New 💬 Ask the Coach panel at the top of the Week view. Tap a suggested chip ("Should I ride today or rest?", "Am I overtraining?", "How is my week going?", "Should I take a recovery day?", "What should I focus on this week?", "Why is my form negative?") or type your own question. The AI receives FULL context: today's plan + weather, what you've already logged today, yesterday's training, your CTL/ATL/TSB fitness curve, body weight trend, last 7 days of gym + Strava rides with TSS, FTP, W/kg, and your goals/level/activities. Response is short (2-3 sentences, ~80 words max) and specifically cites your actual numbers — not generic advice. ACCESS TIERS to control API costs: admin (unlimited, you — ht9323@gmail.com), pro (20/day, trusted users — edit _PRO_EMAILS array to grant), basic (0/day, default — sees a locked teaser). The tier badge appears next to the panel header so you always know your level. Daily counter shown ("3 of 20 left today"). Quota tracked locally and synced via Firebase per signed-in user, resets at midnight local time. Limit-reached state disables the input and shows when access resets. Errors fall back gracefully with the error message inline.

d: Strava ride on a gym day no longer hides the planned gym work — explicit "Replace gym with ride" cascade option
det: Previously: when a Strava ride synced on a planned gym day (e.g., went riding on Pull Tuesday), the week-view row replaced the gym label with the ride name and stats, making it look like the gym day vanished. The plan data was still PULL underneath, but the UI made it invisible. Now: the week-view row keeps showing the gym workout as the primary label (with its colour and icon) and adds a small orange "+ 🚴 X km · Y min logged" line below — both the planned gym and the actual ride are visible. When you open the day, a Strava-ride banner appears at the top with TWO clear actions: "🔄 Replace gym with ride" (cascades the gym workout forward, last gym day in the week becomes REST — mirroring the v2.20 add-workout cascade but in reverse) or "💪 Keep both" (do the gym workout in addition to the ride, prompt is dismissed but ride stays visible as a small inline note). The chosen state persists on the plan day (rideAlongside flag) so re-opens don't re-prompt.

d: Compact "Waiting for Strava" card on ride days + backdate weigh-ins
det: TWO improvements. (1) RIDE-DAY UX — the big 4-field manual ride log form no longer takes up screen space on every ride day when you have Strava connected. Instead a compact single-row card appears with the last sync timestamp, a 🟠 Sync now button, and a 📝 toggle to expand the full manual form if you genuinely want to log without Strava. Future-dated ride days (planned but not yet arrived) hide the manual log form entirely — no point logging a ride that hasn't happened. Once you do tap 📝 to expand, the form stays expanded for the rest of the session. (2) BACKDATE WEIGH-INS — the body weight sheet now has a date picker (defaults to today, max = today, no future dates). Useful for filling in missed days from memory, especially when you want to see the chart appear ASAP after starting to log. Backdated entries write to weight_log at the selected date but only update your "current weight" (used for W/kg) if the selected date is your most recent — so backdating doesn't overwrite a more recent weigh-in.
