d: Group cycling sections under one "🚴 Cycling Performance" header with subtle visual container
det: The Training tab had 4 separate uppercase section headings ("CYCLING PROFILE", "💪 FITNESS · FATIGUE · FORM", "📊 CYCLING PROGRESS", "📈 CYCLING — WEEKLY SUMMARY") which felt redundant and busy. Replaced with one main "🚴 CYCLING PERFORMANCE" header wrapping all 4 subsections in a subtle purple-tinted bordered container. Each subsection now has a smaller inline label inside the container (Profile / 💪 Fitness · Fatigue · Form / 📊 Progress chart / 📈 Weekly summary) so they're still distinguishable but visually subordinate to the main cycling group. Trend metadata that lived in the sub-headers (trend badges, "vs N days ago") is preserved inline next to each sub-label. The logical flow within the group is now Profile (baseline) → Form (current state) → Progress chart (trend) → Weekly summary (volume) — moving from "where I am" to "how I'm changing".

d: Reordered Training tab — daily data up top, config (goals/activities/plan) at the bottom
det: Body Weight is now the very first section under the header — fastest path to log today's weigh-in. Followed by the cycling block (Profile, Fitness, Progress chart, Weekly Summary), then Gym Progress (Tonnage + 1RM), then PRs. The configuration sections (Your Goals, Your Activities, Training Plan / Workout preference) moved to the bottom just above History — you set those once and rarely touch them. Eliminates ~600px of scrolling past static config to reach the daily-action area.

d: FTP estimate transparency sheet — see which rides drove the number, spot missing power data
det: Tapping "📊 Estimate FTP from your rides" no longer shows a generic browser confirm dialog. Instead a proper bottom sheet opens showing the suggested FTP at the top, then a list of the actual rides driving the estimate — each row shows date, duration, NP, the duration adjustment factor applied, and the resulting per-ride FTP estimate. A "Show all eligible rides" toggle expands to every ride considered, sorted by FTP-equivalent NP. If any of your rides ≥30 min lack power data, the sheet shows a warning ("⚠️ N rides skipped — no power data") explaining why HR-only rides can't feed the estimate. This is a transparency tool: if your hardest 1-hour Zone 4 effort isn't in the top-rides list, you immediately know it was an HR-only ride and the auto-estimator couldn't see it — so you can hit ✏️ Set my own value and enter what you actually know your FTP is. Three actions at the bottom: Apply the estimate, Set your own value (opens the manual FTP editor), or Cancel.

d: W/kg bands refined to match Coggan chart precisely — 7 tiers, Untrained tier added
det: Cross-checked the W/kg categorization against the original Coggan/Allen table (from "Training and Racing with a Power Meter") and multiple other sources (Zwift Insider, Cycling Analytics, TrainingPeaks). Refined the male thresholds from 2.0/3.0/4.0/5.0/5.5 to 2.0/2.5/3.2/4.0/5.0/5.5 — adding a distinct "Untrained" tier (< 2.0 W/kg, sedentary or new to cycling) below "Beginner" (2.0-2.5, first few months of regular training). Recreational now starts at 2.5 W/kg (active weekend rider) instead of 2.0. Female bands adjusted similarly (≈0.5 W/kg lower per tier). The W/kg info sheet now shows all 7 tiers.

d: Remove redundant Weight card from Cycling Profile — single source of truth is now Body Weight section
det: The Cycling Profile card showed Weight in the middle column AND the Body Weight section below repeated the same number. Both were already linked to the same profile.weight value, so the Cycling Profile copy was pure duplication. Removed the Weight column. Cycling Profile is now a cleaner 2-column layout (FTP + W/kg), with both cards visually larger (24px numeric values instead of 20px). The W/kg card now shows the calculation breakdown ("125W ÷ 244.1 lb") as a small subtitle so you can verify where the ratio comes from. When weight is unset but FTP is set, the W/kg card displays "Log weight ↓" pointing the user to the Body Weight section. When FTP is unset but weight is set, it says "Set FTP →".

d: W/kg categories now align with Coggan/Allen standard + gender-aware bands + info sheet
det: The W/kg label below the W/KG stat was using overly generous bands ("Recreational" started at 0 W/kg). Corrected to match Coggan & Allen's "Training and Racing with a Power Meter" — the gold-standard reference used by TrainingPeaks, Zwift, and every credible cycling platform. 6 tiers: Beginner / Recreational / Trained / Strong / Cat 1 / Elite or Pro. Bands are now gender-aware — male thresholds at 2.0/3.0/4.0/5.0/5.5 W/kg, female at 1.5/2.5/3.5/4.5/5.0 W/kg (using profile.gender). New ⓘ info button next to "W/KG" opens a sheet showing all 6 bands with ranges, your current tier highlighted, and a note that W/kg matters most on climbs (absolute power matters more on flats due to CdA + drafting).

d: Proper weight entry sheet — number input + lb/kg toggle + live conversion (no more browser prompt)
det: Replaced the browser prompt() dialogs for weight entry with a proper bottom sheet modal matching the app's design language. The sheet has a single large numeric input, two pill toggle buttons (lb / kg) right below, a live conversion line ("≈ 110.7 kg") that updates as you type, and your last weigh-in shown for reference. Switching units mid-entry intelligently converts the current input value so you don't lose your typing. The same sheet is used for logging weigh-ins (from Cycling Profile ✏️ Edit, Body Weight + Log weight, or other entry points) and for setting your goal weight — same unit toggle, same live conversion. Logging a weight from the Cycling Profile card writes to both the current weight (powering W/kg) AND the weight history (powering the Body Weight chart) — so a single entry point updates everything. Clear-current-weight and clear-goal options are available as red secondary buttons on the sheet when there's an existing value to clear.

d: Body weight in lb/kg — flexible input parser, displays follow your unit preference (same setting as gym weights)
det: All body weight inputs and displays now respect the app's unit preference (same setting controls gym weights and body weight — default lb). Weight prompts accept flexible input: bare numbers ("180" or "82") are interpreted in your preferred unit, or you can include an explicit suffix like "180 lb", "82kg", "180 pounds" to override. Editing the Cycling Profile weight stat, logging a daily weigh-in, and setting a goal weight all use the same flexible parser. Storage is always in kg internally so W/kg math stays consistent across the app regardless of display preference. The Body Weight chart Y-axis labels, current value, 90-day change, goal line annotation, slope/week rate, and dot tooltips all render in your preferred unit. Toasts confirm both units after each save (e.g. "Logged 82.5 kg (181.9 lb)") so you can sanity-check the conversion landed where you expected. When viewing in lb, the secondary "kg · logged date" line still shows the kg value for reference.

d: Performance Trends → "Cycling — Weekly Summary": removed gym column (redundant with dedicated Gym Progress section), added TSS column when FTP is set
det: The 4-week trends panel now lives cleanly inside the cycling block as a pure cycling weekly summary. The Gym session-count column was redundant once the dedicated 💪 Gym Progress section with weekly tonnage chart shipped in v2.30. The Gym trend chip was replaced with a Rides chip, and a new TSS column appears in the table whenever FTP is set — surfacing the actual training-stress load per week alongside distance and kJ. Section heading renamed to "Cycling — Weekly Summary" for clarity.

d: Tighten cycling section grouping — remove redundant Fitness/Form hint card when no FTP set
det: The "📊 Unlock training-load tracking" hint card was rendering between the Cycling Profile and the Cycling Progress chart whenever Strava was connected but no FTP was set yet — visually splitting the cycling block. The Cycling Profile card already shows the same "set FTP to unlock" guidance at its bottom, so the duplicate hint card was just clutter. Now when there's no fitness curve yet, the Fitness · Fatigue · Form section renders nothing, and the Cycling Profile sits directly adjacent to the Cycling Progress chart as intended.

d: Auto-estimate FTP from ride data + group cycling sections + hide them when cycling is not selected
det: Three Training tab improvements. (1) FTP is now auto-estimated from your Strava ride NP data using Coggan's intensity model — duration-adjusted top-10% of per-ride NP values: 30-45min × 0.88, 45-75min × 0.95, 75-120min × 1.00, 120+ min × 1.05. Runs automatically on every Strava sync (if you haven't set FTP manually) and on app load. A new ESTIMATED badge replaces the STRAVA/MANUAL tag when the value came from auto-estimation. A new "📊 Estimate FTP from your rides" button appears on the Cycling Profile card whenever you have 3+ qualifying rides — tap to recompute and apply with a confirmation dialog. (2) All cycling sections (Cycling Profile, Fitness · Fatigue · Form, Cycling Progress, Performance Trends) are now grouped together at the top, followed by Body Weight, Gym Progress, then PRs. (3) The cycling block is hidden entirely when "Cycling" is not one of your selected activities — keeps the Training tab clean for gym-only users. Also added a hint explaining why weight can't be auto-derived from ride data (no weight signal in activity objects — needs to be set on Strava profile or entered manually).

d: Gym Progress charts — weekly tonnage with muscle-group split + per-exercise 1RM progression with plateau detection
det: New 💪 Gym Progress section on the Training tab with two charts. (1) Weekly Tonnage: stacked bar chart of total weight × reps across all completed sets, broken down by muscle group (Push / Pull / Legs / Core), last 12 weeks. Trend badge in the header compares recent 4-week average to prior 4-week average. Each bar is tooltipped with the per-group breakdown. (2) Estimated 1RM Progression: pick any exercise from a dropdown (sorted by recent frequency) and see your estimated one-rep max trajectory over 180 days. Uses Epley formula (weight × (1 + reps/30)) on the peak set per session. Shows current, best, and trend rate (kg/lb per month). Dashed regression line indicates direction. Auto-flags plateaus when no new peak 1RM in 21+ days, suggesting a deload or rep-range switch. AI weekly review prompt now receives tonnage trend (recent vs prior 4-week average) and per-exercise 1RM trajectories for your top 6 most-trained lifts, including plateau flags — so coaching advice can reference specific lifts ("your bench has plateaued at 92.5kg for 3 weeks → time for a deload at 85kg × 8").

d: Body weight tracking with chart, goal target, ETA estimate, and AI integration
det: New ⚖️ Body Weight panel on the Training tab logs weigh-ins over time. Tap + Log weight to drop a weigh-in (default: previous value, just nudge the digit). Chart shows raw dots + 7-day rolling average over 90 days, with auto-detected trend rate (kg/week) in the header. Set an optional 🎯 goal weight and a dashed amber line appears on the chart with an estimated "weeks to reach goal" projection based on your current trajectory. 90-day total change shown as a stat above the chart. The existing Cycling Profile ✏️ Edit weight button now also writes to the history log, so manual edits become weigh-ins. Strava's athlete weight is auto-seeded as today's value on first import (unless you've already logged manually). The AI weekly review prompt now receives the full weight context: current value, goal proximity, 7-day and 28-day deltas, rate of change, and healthy cut/bulk reference ranges — so feedback can correlate weight trends with training load (e.g. "you're losing 0.7 kg/week while CTL keeps climbing — sustainable cut" vs "weight dropping but CTL also falling — under-fueling, eat more carbs on ride days").

d: Cycling Progress chart — see fitness trends over 90 days with metric switcher (EF, NP, Power, HR, TSS, Distance, Suffer)
det: A new SVG chart panel on the Training tab plots your last 90 days of rides. Tap chips at the top to switch between 7 metrics: Aerobic Efficiency (W/bpm — the gold-standard endurance fitness indicator, rising = aerobically fitter at the same effort), Normalised Power, Avg Power, Avg HR, TSS per ride, Distance, and Suffer Score. Each ride is a dot, the purple line is a 7-day rolling average for smoothing. The chart auto-picks a sensible default metric based on what data is available (EF if your rides have both power and HR, NP if power-only, HR if neither). A trend badge in the header (↑ IMPROVING / → STABLE / ↓ REGRESSING) uses linear regression across the window — and inverts for HR (lower = improving). Below the chart, first-half vs recent-half averages with a percentage change tell you the magnitude of improvement at a glance.

d: FTP + body weight + IF/TSS per ride + CTL/ATL/TSB fitness curve — proper training-load tracking and richer AI feedback
det: Imports FTP and body weight from Strava's athlete endpoint on connect and every sync (preserves manual overrides — tap ✏️ on the Cycling Profile card to set values manually). With FTP known, every ride now gets an IF (Intensity Factor = NP/FTP) and TSS (Training Stress Score) computed and displayed as a badge on the ride card and history detail. A new Fitness · Fatigue · Form panel on the Training tab shows current CTL (42-day exponential-weighted average TSS — your fitness), ATL (7-day EMA — your fatigue), TSB (CTL−ATL — your form), with a 28-day fitness trend mini-chart and a plain-English interpretation ("Productive training zone" / "Carrying fatigue" etc). 7-day delta indicators show whether fitness is rising or falling. A new Cycling Profile card displays FTP/weight/W·kg⁻¹ with badges showing whether each value came from Strava or was manually set. The AI weekly review prompt now receives the full cycling profile (FTP, weight, W/kg), current CTL/ATL/TSB snapshot with 7-day and 28-day deltas, and per-ride TSS/IF — so feedback can reference your actual training load trajectory ("CTL +6 in 4 weeks is a healthy build, today's ride at IF 0.92 was suprathreshold"). On app load, existing users with an FTP set get IF/TSS backfilled and the curve computed without needing a fresh sync. Disconnecting Strava clears Strava-sourced FTP/weight but preserves manual values.

d: Comprehensive ride metrics in history + 4-week performance trends panel on Training tab
det: History Strava rows now show all captured performance fields in a structured expandable view: power (NP vs avg watts with real/estimated flag, max watts, kJ total), cardio (avg and max HR, suffer score), movement (speed, cadence, elevation), and context (elapsed time, RPE, PR count, workout type badge). The history push is also extended to carry speed, max watts, device_watts flag, RPE, PR count and workout type. A new 4-week Performance Trends panel appears at the top of the Training tab — it shows trend arrows (↑→↓) comparing this week vs 4 weeks ago for distance, training load (kJ), avg NP and gym sessions, plus a compact week-by-week grid showing rides, km, kJ and gym count at a glance. Only shown when Strava ride data is present.

d: Smarter ride adaptation — analyzeStravaAdapt now uses kJ, suffer score and NP instead of duration alone
det: The adaptation engine was only checking two things: did you show up, did you ride long enough. It ignored all quality signals. Rewritten to score each ride on three dimensions: (1) duration — ≥80% of planned time, (2) load quality — kilojoules output vs expected Zone 2 baseline (~9kJ/min), benefit-of-doubt if no power meter, (3) fatigue signal — suffer_score >200 on long rides flags overreaching, NP >25% above avg watts on long rides flags variable-intensity effort (not Zone 2). The factor now has 5 outcomes: overreaching consistently → ease back 0.05, crushing it (comp+quality both high) → pace up 0.08, completing but quality mixed → pace up 0.04, on track → hold, low completion → ease back 0.1. Adaptation detail (completion %, quality %, reason) stored in bike_adapt_detail and shown on the ride day adaptation badge so you can see what drove the change.

d: Richer Strava data — save and display NP, max HR, cadence, kJ, suffer score for better training analysis and AI review
det: Extended the Strava activity field strip to capture 5 training-relevant fields that were previously discarded: weighted_average_watts (Normalized Power — more meaningful than average watts for variable rides), max_heartrate (effort ceiling for zone analysis), average_cadence (pedalling form), kilojoules (total energy output — the real training load number), suffer_score (Strava HR-zone stress score). These are now shown on the ride card (NP with avg watts as sub-label, avg/max HR combined, cadence block, kJ and suffer score as badges) and passed to the AI weekly review prompt so the coach has actual training load data to work with. History tab also carries the new fields. The field strip remains tight — elapsed_time is the only addition without a direct display use but is cheap and meaningful as stopped-time context (elapsed_time − moving_time = rest stops).

d: Fix Strava sync not persisting — strip activities to minimal fields before storing to prevent localStorage quota overflow
det: Raw Strava activity objects include GPS polylines, segment efforts, achievement counts, kudos, best efforts and dozens of other fields. At ~10KB per ride × 200 rides the strava_activities payload can exceed 2MB. DB.set() wraps localStorage.setItem in a silent try/catch, so when the quota is exceeded the data is never actually written, syncUp() then pushes whatever was previously stored (null or stale data), and the next loadFromCloud() overwrites with the stale Firebase snapshot. Fixed by mapping each activity to only the 9 fields the app actually reads: start_date_local, moving_time, distance, average_heartrate, average_watts, total_elevation_gain, name, type, sport_type. 200 rides now takes ~25-35KB instead of 1-3MB. syncUp() is also awaited so Firebase write completes before the success toast appears. Error cases now show a red toast instead of failing silently.

d: Fix Strava rides not persisting across sessions — syncUp() now called after every Strava fetch
det: stravaFetchActivities() was saving rides to localStorage and re-rendering but never calling syncUp(), so the data never reached Firebase. On next app open, loadFromCloud() ran first and overwrote localStorage with the stale Firebase snapshot (no activities), silently wiping the fresh sync. Fixed by adding syncUp() immediately after DB.set(strava_activities). Also added strava_last_sync to the _syncKeys list so the sync timestamp persists too, and fixed stravaDisconnect() which had the same missing syncUp() bug.

d: Smart "Add workout" sheet on ride days — suggests pulling in the next scheduled gym session with a cascade preview; picking a different type auto-resolves week duplicates instead of always cascading
det: The "Add workout" sheet now detects the next scheduled gym day and presents it as the primary suggestion with a coloured card showing the full cascade preview (e.g. Tue → Pull · Wed → Legs · Thu → REST). Confirming the suggestion does the cascade as before. If the user picks any of the other 3 types instead, the week schedule stays untouched but duplicate-resolution runs: any gym day that shares the chosen type with the new extra session gets replaced with whichever of the 4 standard gym types is absent from that week. If no type is missing (5-session edge case), the duplicate is left as-is. If there are no upcoming gym days left in the week, the sheet falls back to showing all 4 types without a suggestion.

d: Add gym session to ride days — tap "+ Add workout" on any ride day to stack a gym session; remaining gym days shift forward automatically
det: Ride days now show a "+ Add workout" button. Tapping it opens a sheet to pick a gym type (Push/Pull/Legs/Upper Pump). The chosen session is stored as extraGym on the plan entry and rendered below the ride card with its exercise list and a separate "Log workout" button. The extra gym log is stored under a separate key (extralog_YYYY-MM-DD) so it never overwrites the ride log. After adding the gym session, all subsequent unlocked gym days in the week cascade forward one slot — the first upcoming gym day gets the second's type, the second gets the third's, and the last becomes REST — so the weekly training volume stays correct. Ride days are never moved. Log saving is now routed through _saveLog() which respects S.activeLogKey so extra gym sets are always persisted to the right key.

d: Fix consecutive ride days — short ride now avoids the day immediately before or after the long ride
det: buildWeek picked the long ride day first (best weather) then picked the short ride day from the remaining candidates penalising only the day after LEGS. There was no penalty for placing the short ride adjacent to the long ride, so Mon long + Tue short (or similar back-to-back pairs) was common. Fixed by computing postLongIdx and preLongIdx after r1 is known, then applying -60 and -40 score penalties respectively when sorting short ride candidates. Day after long ride gets the strongest penalty (-60) since riding hard two days in a row is the worst case; day before gets a moderate penalty (-40). The penalties are soft (not hard exclusions) so in tight weeks with few available days the app can still place them adjacent rather than failing.

d: Fix ride title still showing "Short Ride"/"Long Ride" — title now shows actual session name (Sweet Spot, Tempo Intervals, etc)
det: The WI label (wi.l) for ride types was still returning the generic "Short Ride"/"Long Ride" i18n string even after v2.17 made the description dynamic. Updated wi.l to also call getRideSession() so the week row title now shows the actual session name. Description updated to show duration + ride category (Zone 2 for long rides, Quality/Recovery for short rides) without redundantly repeating the name.

d: Fix ride plan showing wrong info — week view now shows actual session name and duration from the structured plan, not hardcoded "25–35 min · Zone 2"
det: The WI (workout info) object had hardcoded descriptions for ride types ("25–35 min · Zone 2 · Outdoor", "60–90 min · Zone 2 · Outdoor") that bore no relation to the actual planned sessions. The real planner (getRideSession) builds structured workouts — Tempo Intervals (55 min), Sweet Spot (60 min), Hill Repeats (55 min), Recovery Spin (35 min), Endurance Ride (duration adapts based on setup + Strava adapt factor) — but this info never made it to the week view row or day screen hero. Fixed by making the WI descriptions dynamic functions that call getRideSession() so the week row now shows e.g. "Tempo Intervals · 55 min · Outdoor" instead of "25–35 min · Zone 2". Also added a Strava adaptation badge (Pacing up / Easing back) on the ride card when bike_adapt_factor is meaningfully away from 1.0, so users can see the plan is reacting to their Strava history.

d: 3 new features: Assisted Pull-Up + Assisted Dip exercises, Weekly AI Review enabled (exercise type/sequence recs based on goal), End-of-week prompt to plan next week with AI weight/rep suggestions per exercise
det: (1) Added Assisted Pull-Up and Assisted Dip to the exercise database as machine-based alternatives to Pull-Ups and Tricep Dips. Both are added to their respective SLOTS arrays so they surface as swap alternatives. (2) Enabled the Weekly AI Review feature (FEATURE_WEEKLY_REVIEW=true). The review prompt now includes user goal and fitness level, and adds a 5th SEQUENCE section with exercise type and sequencing advice. (3) After completing all exercises in your last gym session of the week, an end-of-week prompt appears asking if you want AI to plan next week. If confirmed, AI reviews your week's performance and generates next week's plan with per-exercise starting weight and rep suggestions. Suggestions are pre-filled in your workout logs for next week.

d: Fix login hanging in Safari — set Firebase auth persistence to LOCAL
det: Safari's Intelligent Tracking Prevention (ITP) blocks the hidden cross-origin iframe that Firebase Auth uses to restore sessions and complete sign-in. This caused login to hang indefinitely in Safari while working fine in Chrome. Fixed by explicitly calling setPersistence(LOCAL) when Firebase initialises, which forces Firebase to use localStorage for auth state instead of the iframe/cookie mechanism. This is the standard fix for Firebase + Safari.

d: Sign-in field label changed to "Username"
Sign-up now uses username instead of email — simpler and no more derivation issues
det: The sign-up form showed "Email" which caused users to enter their full email address (e.g. helenlenlau@gmail.com). The code then had to strip the domain and special characters to derive a username, which was confusing and error-prone. Changed sign-up to ask for a plain username (letters, numbers, _ only — no @ allowed). Sign-in still accepts username or email for existing users. Added validation: min 3 chars, no @ allowed on sign-up, clear hint text under the field.

d: Sign in / sign up no longer hang forever on bad connections
det: Firebase auth calls (signInWithEmailAndPassword and createUserWithEmailAndPassword) had no timeout — on a slow or flaky connection they would spin on "..." indefinitely with no feedback. Added a 12-second timeout to both: if Firebase doesn't respond within 12s the user sees "Connection timed out — check your internet and try again." and the button re-enables so they can retry.

d: Fix 4 signup bugs: mangled username, orphaned accounts, missing rules guidance, login hang
det: (1) Username was derived from the full email including domain — helenlenlau@gmail.com became "helenlenlaugmailcom". Fixed to extract only the local part before @, giving "helenlenlau". (2) Firebase rules for /usernames/ were missing entirely — added to docs and the rules block is now in the setup guide. (3) If auth account creation succeeded but the DB transaction failed (network drop etc), the auth account became orphaned — user gets email-already-in-use on retry with no recovery path. Improved the error message to explain the situation and guide toward password reset. (4) loadFromCloud() after signup had no timeout — could leave the user stuck on the loading button forever. Added an 8s timeout so the app always proceeds.

d: Fix account creation error: permission_denied when signing up
det: Creating an account was failing with "permission_denied at /usernames/..." for new users. Root cause: the code was reading /usernames/ to check if the username was taken BEFORE creating the Firebase Auth account — so the user was unauthenticated and Firebase blocked the read. Fixed by creating the auth account first, then using a Firebase transaction to atomically claim the username while authenticated. The transaction aborts if the username is already taken, rolls back the auth account, and shows the "already taken" message. This also makes the username claim atomic, preventing two users from racing to claim the same username.

d: Swipe-back: eliminate lag — pre-build behind layer at touchstart, cache DOM refs
det: The lag in v2.07/2.08 had two causes: (1) rWeek() + innerHTML was called on the first touchmove frame, causing a visible jank spike right as the drag started. Moved to touchstart so the DOM work is done before any finger movement. (2) The parallax behind element had transition:0.1s which fought against direct style updates every frame, making it sluggish. Removed the transition entirely — parallax is now a direct assignment each frame. (3) document.querySelector was being called on every touchmove event — replaced with cached sEl/behindEl references stored in the _sb state object. Behind layer now starts fully transparent (opacity:0) and fades in as you drag, which also looks better.

d: Swipe-back: fix workout page losing background + vertical scroll during drag
det: Two bugs from v2.07: (1) The .screen element had no background colour set, so as it slid right the week view injected behind it was visible through the page — the workout appeared to lose its background. Fixed by adding background:var(--bg) to .screen. (2) The touchmove listener was passive:true so the browser could still scroll the page vertically while a horizontal drag was in progress. Fixed by attaching a non-passive touchmove listener (with preventDefault) only for the duration of an active horizontal tracking session — it is added when tracking starts and removed immediately on touchend/touchcancel/cancel, so scroll performance everywhere else is unaffected.

d: Swipe-back: week view now visible behind the workout page as you drag
det: Previously the area behind the sliding workout page was black (just the app background). Now when you start swiping right, the week view is rendered behind the current screen immediately. As you drag, it scales up from 95% to 100% and fades from 70% to full opacity — the same parallax depth effect iOS uses. On release: if you commit, the behind element is removed and the week view appears; if you cancel, the behind element is removed and the workout page snaps back. No jank: the week HTML is generated once when tracking starts and reused for the entire gesture.

d: Swipe-back is now interactive — page follows your finger like Safari
det: Rewrote the gesture from a trigger-and-animate model to a true finger-following model. The workout page now moves with your finger in real-time as you swipe right, with a growing left-edge shadow for depth. On release: if you committed (strong flick or past 40% screen width) the page slides off to the right and the week view appears; if you released early the page springs back to its original position. Vertical scroll intent is detected early and cancels the gesture immediately so scrolling in workouts still works. Activation thresholds are unchanged from v2.05.

d: Swipe-back activation toned down further
det: Raised thresholds again: quick-flick now requires 80px travel (was 50px) at velocity >0.65 px/ms (was 0.5), and slow-drag requires 160px (~40% of screen width, was 120px). The gesture should now only fire on a clear, strong intentional swipe.

d: Swipe-back requires a more deliberate swipe to activate
det: The gesture was firing too easily on accidental brushes. Raised the quick-flick threshold from 25px to 50px travel (and velocity from 0.4 to 0.5 px/ms), and the slow-drag threshold from 70px to 120px (~quarter of the screen width). You now need a clear intentional swipe to go back rather than a small nudge.

d: Fix wrong week on open, bottom nav bar out of place, and swipe-back too fast
det: Three fixes: (1) On weekends, init() was advancing weekStart to next Monday — removed that logic so the app always opens on the current week. (2) The nav slide animations used will-change:transform,opacity which creates a CSS stacking context, causing position:fixed on the bottom nav bar to anchor to the .screen element instead of the viewport, making it appear in the wrong place after any navigation animation. Fixed by removing will-change from the animation CSS and adding an animationend listener to strip the animation class as soon as it finishes. Also removed dead sb-slide-off-right/sb-slide-in-from-left keyframes and .sb-animating-out/.sb-behind-anim classes left over from v2.00. (3) Nav transition duration increased from 300ms to 420ms and slide distance from 22% to 35% — the previous values made the transition barely perceptible; the new values match iOS native navigation feel.

d: Swipe-back diagnostic toast removed now that the gesture is confirmed working
det: v2.01 added a green debug toast on every detected swipe to verify the gesture was firing. User confirmed the swipe + animation works end-to-end, so the toast is no longer needed. Removed in this version for a clean, silent gesture experience. The simplified animation approach (using the existing .nav-back slide-in keyframes that the back button also uses) is the keeper.

d: Swipe-back simplified to use the existing back-button animation + diagnostic toast to verify the gesture is even being detected
det: After six failed attempts (v1.96 through v2.00) to get a two-screen swipe animation working on iPhone, ripped out all the custom code and made the swipe gesture do exactly the same thing as tapping the back button: render the week view with the existing .nav-back CSS slide-in animation (which already works — you can see it when you tap the back button). The trade-off: only the new screen animates in from the left, the workout page doesn't slide off to the right. But that is far better than zero animation. Also added a green debug toast on every detected swipe showing the measured dx and velocity, so we can confirm in your next test whether the gesture is firing at all — if you see the toast but no animation, the issue is somewhere in the rendering path; if you do not see the toast, the gesture detection itself is broken.

d: Swipe-back animation rewritten with CSS @keyframes — fixes the long-running issue where the workout page wasn't actually animating
det: After three attempts to fix the swipe-back animation with CSS transitions (v1.96, v1.97, v1.99) the workout page was still not moving. Switched to CSS @keyframes which have explicit from/to states baked in — no inline transform timing tricks, no double-rAF dance, no transitionend race conditions. The outgoing screen gets a class with animation: sb-slide-off-right which animates from translate3d(0,0,0) to translate3d(100vw,0,0). The destination (week view) is layered behind with its own animation from translate3d(-100vw,0,0) to translate3d(0,0,0). Both slide a full screen width across (was only 25% before, which was too subtle to see clearly). Cleanup happens on the animationend event when the outgoing screen finishes, with a 500ms setTimeout safety net. Also bumped to v2.00 as a milestone — this should be the last gesture-related fix.

d: Swipe-back animation actually visible now — workout page slides off to the right instead of just teleporting away
det: Diagnosed from the video: the wrap (week view behind) was animating correctly because its initial transform was set explicitly, but the workout page itself was not animating because I never set its initial transform, and browsers (especially iOS Safari) fail to animate a transform change when the previous value was the "none" keyword instead of an actual transform value. The result was: workout sits still for 300ms while the wrap silently slides in behind it (invisible because the workout was layered on top), then setTimeout fires and replaces the workout with the week view — looking like an instant teleport. Fixed by explicitly setting transform:translate3d(0,0,0) on the workout page before the transition, forcing a layout commit with getBoundingClientRect, using a double requestAnimationFrame to ensure the transition is registered before the transform changes, and switching from setTimeout-based cleanup to the transitionend event so cleanup happens after the animation actually finishes (with a setTimeout fallback in case transitionend never fires).

d: Swipe-back rewritten with velocity detection — no more finger-dragging, just flick right and the page slides off cleanly
det: Watched a screen recording of v1.97 and saw the problem: the finger-follow approach made the gesture feel sluggish during slow swipes (the screen literally only moved as much as the user's finger did, which on a slow drag is barely any) and required a long deliberate drag to commit. Replaced the entire gesture with a velocity + distance trigger model: tracks finger velocity via an exponential moving average; once velocity exceeds 0.4 px/ms with at least 25px traveled (a quick flick) OR a slower drag passes 70px (deliberate), the back animation fires. The animation is now a clean 300ms slide-off — the workout page glides to the right with a drop shadow while the week view parallaxes in from the left. No more finger-dragging. This matches how React Native's default navigation handles back-swipe, not Safari's exact gesture, but feels far more responsive on iPhone. Layout commit is forced with offsetWidth + the transform change is deferred via requestAnimationFrame so the transition always actually plays.

d: Swipe-back fix: slow swipes no longer get stuck mid-screen — release now always smoothly commits or snaps back
det: In v1.96 a slow swipe would visually move the workout page with your finger but then "stick" at the release point without animating to commit or snap-back. Root cause: when transition was set to "none" during the drag, then both transition and transform were changed in the same synchronous block at touchend, the browser would skip the animation and either jump instantly to the end state or appear frozen. Fixed by separating the transition change from the transform change with requestAnimationFrame and a forced layout commit (offsetWidth read) in between — the browser registers the new transition value before the transform changes, so the animation actually plays. Also: activation threshold dropped from 12px to 8px (more responsive feedback), commit threshold dropped from 35% to 30% of screen width (easier to complete), commit duration scales with drag distance so a near-full swipe finishes faster than a partial one.

d: Safari-style interactive swipe-back — current page follows your finger, week view peeks in from the left with parallax + drop shadow
det: The previous version just played a slide-in animation after a swipe completed, which is why it still felt jumpy. This release rewrites the gesture as a real interactive drag: when you start swiping right inside a workout, the week view is pre-rendered behind the current page, then both pages move together while your finger is on the screen. The current page tracks 1:1 with your finger and has a soft drop shadow on its left edge; the week view behind it parallax-scrolls in from -25% to 0% as you drag, matching iOS Safari's native behavior. Release past 35% of the screen width commits the navigation (smooth 280ms ease-out completion); release before that snaps both pages back to their starting positions. The previous slide-in animation is suppressed during a completed swipe (via a new _noAnim option on go()) so you don't see two animations stacked. Activation only fires after 12px of clear horizontal motion, so vertical scrolling through long workouts doesn't accidentally trigger it.

d: Smooth iOS-style slide transitions on navigation — back-and-forward now actually feels like a real app
det: Previously every screen change was an instant innerHTML swap with zero animation, which felt jarring even when the data was right. Added two CSS keyframe animations on the .screen container: nav-fwd slides in from the right when you drill into a workout from the week view, nav-back slides in from the left when you swipe right or tap the back button. 300ms with an iOS-style ease curve (cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1)). The go() function now accepts a _dir option that applies the matching class to the freshly rendered screen. All back buttons (← Week, ← Back) and the swipe-right gesture pass _dir:back; tapping into a day passes _dir:fwd. Also added a window.scrollTo(0,0) on every navigation so the new screen always opens at the top instead of inheriting the previous screen's scroll position. Respects prefers-reduced-motion for accessibility.

d: Swipe-right to go back (matches iOS convention) — previously had the direction inverted
det: Earlier versions implemented swipe LEFT to go back based on a wording miscommunication. iOS uses swipe RIGHT as its universal back gesture (Safari, Mail, Messages, every native and web app). Flipped the detection: a clear swipe to the right inside a workout now navigates back to the week view. Threshold widened slightly to 60px of vertical tolerance now that we are matching user muscle memory.

d: Sticky back button in workouts — the back arrow now stays pinned to the top of the screen as you scroll through exercises
det: The v1.92 debug toast revealed why swipe-left was never triggering: real "swipes" on a scrollable workout list end up dominated by vertical motion (dy ~240px vs dx ~50px). Tuning thresholds wasn't going to fix that — the only reliable solution is a back button that's always visible. The day header (← Week  ·  Sat 23  ·  Swap ↕) is now sticky-positioned with a translucent backdrop blur, so it follows the page as you scroll. The swipe-left gesture still exists as a power-user shortcut, but it now requires a very horizontal swipe (90px+ left, <50px of vertical drift, completed in <600ms). Debug toast removed.

d: Swipe-back diagnostic build — added pointer-event fallback, broadened thresholds, and a temporary debug toast that shows the measured swipe values on every touch
det: The swipe-left-to-go-back gesture still wasn't triggering on iPhone after the screen-name fix in v1.91. This release attaches the listener to window (not document) and adds a parallel pointer-event listener as a fallback path in case iOS isn't bubbling touch events the way we expected. Distance threshold lowered to 60px, time window widened to 800ms, horizontal-vs-vertical ratio relaxed to 1.2:1. Debug toast is temporarily enabled so any swipe with dx or dy >25px shows the actual measured values — green if it would have triggered back navigation, gray if it didn't. Use this to tell us whether the gesture is being detected at all, and if so what the measurements look like. Will remove the debug toast in 1.93 once we know what's happening.

d: Bulletproof cross-device sync, swipe-left to leave a workout, tap-to-sync on Account, and a stack of plan/advisor fixes
det: Sync now actually works on every app open — a long-standing bug meant returning users never re-pulled from Firebase because S.authed was set early by init() before the auth listener fired. Added a four-layer auto-sync system: instant Firebase listener while active, foreground refresh when the PWA wakes from background, 60-second polling safety net, and an online-event trigger when the network reconnects. The Account section now folds the sync status, last-pulled timestamp, and error display into one block — tap the green card to manually push+pull on demand. Removed the redundant JSON backup/import (cloud sync replaces them; import was actually dangerous because it could overwrite synced data) and the dead "Feedback & Wishlist coming soon" section. Inside a workout, swiping left anywhere on the page now navigates back to the week view — the screen identifier was "day" not "log" so the original gesture never fired. Other fixes shipped this round: regenerate plan now locks any day with completed sets (was relying solely on per-set done flags and could overwrite logged workouts); filterSlot now prefers gym exercises and only falls back to bodyweight when no gym option exists (was mixing push-ups into your GoodLife Push days); weekly advisor now sends planned exercises for upcoming sessions plus the best set from history, with rules to suggest +2.5 of weight or +1 rep targets across every upcoming exercise; exercise-swap now pushes to Firebase (was localStorage-only); subtle "Synced 2m ago" indicator on the Week view footer.

d: Cycling preference tabs moved to My Training — week view decluttered, Regenerate shortcut added to header
det: The three cycling mode buttons (Outdoor + Gym / Indoor + Gym / Gym only) have been moved from the week view into a new Training Plan section on the My Training tab. They were only useful once at initial setup and were cluttering the week screen on every visit. A 🔄 icon in the week-nav header now lets you regenerate the current plan without scrolling. The week view empty state is simplified — it just shows a Generate button and points to My Training to change the cycling preference.

d: Advisor exercise swap suggestions — AI recommends specific exercise changes, wired directly into your workout
det: The Weekly Advisor now outputs a SWAPS section alongside TARGETS. When the AI spots stalled progress on an exercise (3+ sessions with no weight or rep improvement), a missing movement pattern for your goal, or a clearly better alternative for your level — it flags it with a specific swap: e.g. "Switch Lying Leg Curl → Nordic Curl — better eccentric hamstring load". That suggestion appears as an amber badge inside the exercise card when you open it in your workout. One tap on Swap → applies it immediately to your session and plan, exactly like the existing machine-busy swap. The sequencing research (NSCA compound-before-isolation guidelines, agonist-antagonist pairing for Upper Pump) is also documented inline in the slot templates.

d: Exercise sequencing overhaul — proper movement order and slot logic for all workout types
det: Four fixes to how sessions are built. (1) PUSH: shoulder compound (OHP/DB press) was sitting in slot 3, after chest accessories — it now comes immediately after flat bench as slot 2, which is the standard push protocol. (2) PULL: had two separate bicep slots meaning every pull session forced two bicep exercises. Merged into one slot — biceps already get significant work from all the rows. (3) LEGS: BSS, lunges, and step-ups (heavy unilateral compound movements) were in slot 3 alongside leg press and leg extension. Moved all unilateral compounds to slot 1/3 properly — slot 3 is now secondary compound and machine work, slot 4 is pure isolation. (4) Sort bug: the exercise variety sort had ai-bi inverted — it was silently picking the MOST recently used exercise each time instead of the least recently used. Fixed to bi-ai so the app correctly rotates exercises across sessions.

d: Fix advisor cross-device trigger + merge AI usage counts across devices
det: Two sync fixes. (1) The advisor was saving to its own Firebase path but never updating the users/{uid}/updated timestamp, so the cross-device listener on other devices never fired. Fixed by re-adding a saveToCloud() call after advisor generates (updates the timestamp), and extending the sync listener to also pull the current week advisor from Firebase when it wakes up. (2) AI usage log was never synced — each device had its own count. Added ai_usage to the sync bundle, and changed loadFromCloud to merge the calls arrays by timestamp union rather than blindly overwriting — so both devices end up with the combined total.

d: Weekly Advisor cross-device sync — fix Firebase array conversion + dedicated storage path
det: v1.85 had two silent bugs. (1) The PC PWA was cached on v1.84 when the fix shipped, so weekly_advisor_* keys were never included in the Firebase save. (2) Firebase Realtime Database converts JavaScript arrays to objects with numeric keys on round-trip — so even if the data synced, the targets array came back as {"0":{...}} instead of [{...}], breaking the target lookup silently. Fixed by: storing the advisor result directly at users/{uid}/advisor/{weekKey} as a JSON string (strings round-trip perfectly through Firebase), checking that path first on any device before hitting the API, and falling back to the AI only when Firebase has nothing. This means generate-once-use-everywhere with no wasted API calls.

d: Weekly Advisor syncs to Firebase — generate once, available on all your devices
det: The weekly advisor result (including Smart Targets) was previously stored only in localStorage, meaning each device had to make its own API call. Now weekly_advisor_* keys are included in the Firebase sync bundle. As soon as the advisor generates on any device, it saves to the cloud and your other devices pick it up automatically via the existing cross-device listener — no extra API calls needed.

d: Smart Targets — Weekly Advisor now sets exercise targets that appear in your workout log
det: The Weekly Advisor now outputs a structured TARGETS block alongside its text advice. When you open an exercise that has a specific target this week (e.g. "Lying Leg Curl at 130lbs × 12"), a green 🎯 badge appears in the exercise body showing exactly what to aim for. When you complete all sets on that exercise, the app checks your best set against the target: hit it and you get a "Target achieved!" toast; close but not quite gets an encouraging nudge. Targets are extracted by the AI from the FOCUS section using the exact exercise names in your training data, so they only appear for exercises the AI actually mentioned.

d: Handle Gemini 503 overload — better error messages for all AI failure types
det: Gemini occasionally returns 503 (temporarily overloaded) in addition to 429 (quota) and 403 (auth). The Cloudflare Worker now falls through to the next provider on 503 as well. The app now distinguishes three error states: quota exhausted (no retry, reset at midnight), overloaded (retry shown, "usually clears in a minute"), and connection blip (retry shown). Previously 503 looked the same as a connection blip with no explanation.

d: Weekly Advisor: workout names now human-readable instead of raw code
det: The AI was receiving internal type constants like UPPER_PUMP, PUSH, PULL, LONG_OUTDOOR in the prompt and echoing them back verbatim in the advice. Added a type label map so the AI always receives plain English names — "Upper Body (Full Upper)", "Push (Chest/Shoulders/Triceps)", "Long Outdoor Ride" etc. Both the training history and the upcoming schedule sections of the prompt are now translated.

d: Body stats added to profile — weight, height, age fed to AI coach
det: Added weight, height, and age fields to the profile setup (step 3 — Last few details). Both weight and height have kg/lb and cm/ft unit toggles. A privacy notice explains the data is stored privately in your account and never shared with friends or used outside your own training coach. All three values are now passed to the Weekly Advisor and Gym Coach AI prompts so the AI can calibrate intensity, suggest appropriate loading, and factor in body composition when giving advice (e.g. strength-to-body-weight ratios, appropriate cardio intensity for weight loss goals).

d: Friends — connect with friends and see each other's weekly training
det: Added a full friends system. Each user gets a unique 6-character friend code (e.g. A3K9P2) generated at login. Share your code — your friend enters it to send a request. You get a red badge on the Settings tab when a request comes in. Accept or decline inline. Once connected, you see each other's Strava-style weekly card: a 7-dot Mon–Sun activity strip, session counts (gym + rides), total km, and week streak. No weights or PRs are shared — just the summary. Week summary is written to Firebase on every save so friends always see current data. Friend codes are stored in a reverse-lookup table so there's no searching the user database.

d: Rest days no longer show "How are you feeling?"
det: The energy selector (Fresh / Okay / Tired / Sore) is only relevant before a training session. On REST & MOBILITY days it served no purpose and added noise. It is now hidden on rest days — only shown on gym and ride days where the coach uses it to adjust your session targets.

d: Auth: fix half-stuck accounts + smarter error messages
det: Fixed a scenario where a user (e.g. on a restricted network) could start creating an account, have the network drop mid-way, and then be permanently stuck — unable to create (email already in use) or sign in (unknown password). Now: auth/email-already-in-use shows inline "Sign in instead" and "Reset your password" action buttons. Wrong-password errors on sign-in now show an inline "Forgot password?" link. Added the modern auth/invalid-login-credentials error code to the map (Firebase changed this code and it was falling through to a raw ugly error message). Added auth/network-request-failed with a clear connection error message.

d: Weekly Advisor: smarter context for new users + better PR labels
det: Two improvements to the Weekly Advisor. (1) The advisor now counts how many weeks of gym history exist in the app and passes that context to the AI — on week 1 it explicitly tells the AI these are baseline measurements, not progressions, so it stops saying "excellent progression" when everything is a first-time entry. (2) PR labels in the training data sent to the AI now distinguish between [baseline — first logged], [NEW PR], and [below PR: X×Y] so the AI has real signal about whether a number is a first-time baseline, a genuine new personal record, or a below-best session.

d: Code cleanup — quota-error helper, stale-flag fix
det: Internal code review cleanup. (1) The 429/403 quota-error check was copy-pasted in 4 places — now a single isQuotaErr() helper. (2) Fixed a bug where the "AI quota used up" note could linger all session: the _aiQuotaHit flag now clears automatically as soon as any AI call succeeds again. (3) Removed redundant comments.

d: AI Usage dashboard in Settings — see calls today, this week, by type, and quota bar
det: Added a full AI usage tracker. Every Gemini call (Gym Coach, Ride Coach, Weekly Advisor, Weekly Review) is logged to localStorage with timestamp and success/fail status. The Settings tab now shows: Today / This week / All time counts, a daily quota progress bar vs the ~1500/day free tier limit, a 7-day bar chart, a breakdown by feature type, and the last call time. A Clear button resets the log. Quota warning appears when >85% of daily limit is used.

d: AI quota awareness — clear messages when daily limit is hit
det: When Gemini's free-tier daily quota is exhausted (403/429), the app now shows a specific message: "Daily AI quota is used up — resets at midnight Pacific time" instead of a generic error. The Weekly Advisor hides the retry button (no point retrying until quota resets). The AI Coach shows a small note below the default tip. A global _aiQuotaHit flag is set by any AI call so all components respond consistently.

d: Cross-device sync — plan and log data now syncs live between your phone and PC
det: Added a Firebase real-time listener that watches for changes from other devices. When you log a session or generate a plan on your phone, your PC picks it up automatically (and vice versa) without needing to reload the app. Uses the existing Firebase Realtime Database — no new setup required. A "Synced from another device" toast appears when remote data is pulled in.

d: Weekly Advisor: fix silent API errors + human-friendly messages
det: Two improvements to the Weekly Advisor. (1) API errors were being swallowed and mis-reported as "not enough data" — now errors propagate correctly so the right message is shown. (2) All advisor states now use plain human language: connection failures say "might just be a blip", genuinely empty data shows a first-week welcome, and the idle state is shorter and friendlier.

d: Fix: duplicate Monday row; Weekly Advisor shows error state instead of silent failure
det: Two fixes. (1) A bug could produce duplicate day entries in the plan (two Monday rows). Now deduplicated at render time so only the first entry per date is shown. (2) The Weekly Advisor "Analyse" button was failing silently — if the API returned no data or errored, the card just stayed empty with no feedback. Now shows a specific error message ("not enough data" vs "connection failed") with a retry button, and a success toast when the analysis completes.

d: Weekly Advisor added — AI analysis of your training with weekly focus points
det: A new 🧠 Weekly Advisor card now appears on the week plan screen. Tap "Analyse my training" and Gemini reviews the last 2 weeks of your actual logged data — gym sets/weights/reps per exercise, Strava rides with HR and power — and returns 4 specific points: Training Load (volume assessment), Trend (what the numbers show — flagging fatigue, progression, plateaus by name), Focus (specific targets for this week), and Recovery (readiness note). Cached per week so it does not re-fetch on every render. Refresh button available to re-run the analysis.

d: Weather refresh preserves exercises; AI Coach uses real training data
det: Two major upgrades. (1) "Refresh with new weather" now only reschedules which days are rides, gym, or rest — it no longer regenerates exercise selections if the session type is unchanged. Your workout content survives a weather refresh. (2) AI Coach is now data-driven: ride days get coaching based on your last 8 Strava rides (HR, watts, distance trends) with specific targets; gym days now show 4-week set/rep trends per exercise so the coach can flag fatigue (dropped reps), plateaus, or PR opportunities with exact numbers.

d: Plan now uses your goal and Strava rides to decide how many ride days to schedule
det: Previously the planner always assigned exactly 2 ride days regardless of what you already rode or what your goal is. Now: (1) Your profile goal drives the ride quota — endurance/performance goals get more ride days, muscle goals get mostly gym, fitness goals get a balanced split. (2) Strava rides already done this week count toward that quota first — if you rode Monday and Thursday and your target is 2 rides, no more rides are added to the remaining days.

d: Past weeks with no plan now auto-show recorded Strava rides and gym sessions
det: Navigating to a previous week that had no generated plan used to show the empty "Ready to generate" screen even if you had Strava rides or logged gym sessions that week. Now the app scans strava_activities and gym log keys for that date range and renders whatever was recorded automatically — no generate needed. A "Generate plan for this week" button still appears below.

d: Strava history extended to 6 months; history panel extended to 180 days
det: Strava sync was only fetching 8 weeks of rides with a 100-activity cap. Bumped to 180 days and per_page=200 (Strava API max) so older rides appear in workout history. The workout history panel in My Training was also extended from 90 to 180 days to match.

d: Strava ride name always shown on plan day rows, not just on unplanned days
det: When a Strava ride was recorded on a planned ride day (Long Ride, Short Ride), the plan row kept showing the generic plan name instead of the actual Strava activity name. Fixed — the Strava ride name and stats now always take priority over the planned label.

d: Service worker cache busted; EMountainBikeRide added to ride type filter
det: The service worker was serving a stale cached index.html so recent fixes (v1.62/1.63 Strava plan row changes) were not reaching users. Bumped cache to tb-v3 to force a fresh load. Also added EMountainBikeRide and EBikeSport to the Strava ride type filter so e-bike rides are always captured on sync.

d: Strava days labelled "Logged · Strava" on the week plan
det: Any day with a Strava ride now shows an orange "🟠 Logged · Strava" badge on the plan row, making it immediately clear which days were recorded via Strava.

d: Strava rides now show on plan day rows; unplanned rides override rest/gym label
det: When a Strava ride is recorded on any day — including rest days or gym days — the week plan now replaces that day's label with the ride name, distance, and duration, and marks it with an orange Strava badge. Rides on planned rest days (like an unplanned Monday ride) are fully surfaced in the plan view.

d: Past days are now greyed out in the week view
det: Days before today now appear at reduced opacity, matching the same faded treatment used for completed days. Today stays full brightness with the purple border and upcoming days remain fully visible.

d: Strava rides now appear in workout history
det: Strava activities were stored in strava_activities but never shown in the My Training history tab. The history scan now includes rides from the past 90 days alongside gym sessions, sorted newest-first. Each ride shows the activity name, distance, duration, heart rate, watts, and elevation gain with an orange Strava badge.

d: Plan order fixed; Strava rides now lock completed days on refresh
det: Two fixes. (1) The lock logic that preserves completed days on refresh was keyed by array position, not by date — so a previously corrupted plan (with wrong order) would scramble the new plan. It is now keyed by date string so position never matters. The day list is also sorted by date at render time as a final safety net. (2) Completed Strava rides now lock ride days the same way completed gym sessions lock gym days — refreshing the plan will no longer overwrite a day you already rode.

d: "Sync now" button added to ride card; Garmin ride types now recognised
det: When Strava is connected but no activity has synced for a ride day yet, the ride log card now shows a "🟠 Sync now · Synced Xm ago" button so you can trigger a fresh Strava fetch without leaving the day screen. Also widened the ride type filter to include GravelRide, MountainBikeRide, EBikeRide and sport_type variants — Garmin can produce any of these and they were previously ignored.

d: Fix: "Refresh with new weather" now always fetches fresh data and never drops days
det: Two fixes. (1) Clicking "Refresh with new weather" was still returning a stale cached result if you had refreshed in the last 3 hours — including bad cached results from before the v1.56 fix. The explicit refresh button now always bypasses the weather cache and forces a fresh API call. (2) buildWeek now has a safety net: if the weather array arrives with fewer than 7 days for any reason, it pads the missing days from the existing plan or a neutral placeholder, so a partial result can never produce a short week.

d: Fix: refreshing plan mid-week no longer drops past days from the week view
det: When you refreshed the plan on Wednesday, Monday and Tuesday disappeared. Root cause: the Open-Meteo weather API only returns forecast data from today onwards — so looking up Monday on a Wednesday returned nothing, and the plan was built starting from Wednesday. Fixed by building all 7 days from the Monday start date individually, falling back to the existing plan's weather data for any past day (or a neutral placeholder if there is no prior data). Refreshing on any day of the week now always produces a complete Mon–Sun week.

d: Bodyweight exercise images: 14 of 18 now show real demos instead of placeholders
det: Added a second image source (wger.de) for exercises missing from the free-exercise-db. Push-Up, Diamond Push-Up, Inverted Row, Donkey Kick now pull from wger.de. Bicycle Crunch and Floor Leg Raise have 2-frame animations. Combined with the 8 already fixed in v1.54, 14 of the 18 bodyweight exercises now show real images. The remaining 4 (Pike Push-Up, Wall Sit, Side Plank, Burpee) have no suitable image in either database and show styled muscle-group placeholders. The image loader now supports both free-exercise-db folder paths and direct wger.de URLs.

d: "At home today" moved to each workout day — now per-day, instant, no regenerate needed
det: "Training from home this week?" has been redesigned. Instead of a week-wide toggle on the Plan tab that required a separate Regenerate tap, there is now a compact "Training at home today?" row on each individual gym day screen. Tap it and the exercises switch to bodyweight immediately — no second step. Tap it again to switch back to gym exercises. It only affects that one day. Also fixed: 8 of the 18 bodyweight exercises now show real demo images (Decline Push-Up, Superman, Bodyweight Squat, Jump Squat, Bodyweight Lunge, Single-Leg Glute Bridge, Mountain Climber, Crunch) — the remaining 10 show styled muscle-group placeholders since those specific movements are not in the exercise image database.

d: Settings Account section layout fixes — no empty space, clearer button labels
det: "Sign out" no longer sits in a half-empty two-column row. "Backup (.json)" renamed to "Download backup" — the .json detail was meaningless to most people.

d: iPhone home screen icon updated to the current app logo
det: The apple-touch-icon (the icon shown when you add Training Brain to your iPhone home screen) was still the original placeholder. It now uses the same logo shown inside the app. To see the update: remove the existing home screen shortcut and re-add it via Safari → Share → Add to Home Screen.

d: Backup status now lives inside the Account card in Settings
det: The backup status row (green dot, "Backed up X ago", "Back up now") is now grouped inside the Account card under Settings → Account & Backup, separated by a subtle divider below the signed-in name. It was previously floating as a standalone bar at the top of Settings. This keeps all account and backup actions in one place.

d: Plan mode labels clarified — Outdoor + Gym, Indoor + Gym, Gym only
det: The three plan modes have been renamed to be self-explanatory. "Use weather" is now "Outdoor + Gym" — it schedules outdoor cardio on the best weather days and gym on the rest. "Indoor only" is now "Indoor + Gym" — trainer or Zwift sessions indoors plus gym, weather ignored. "No biking" / "Gym only" keeps the same meaning but is now clearly labelled everywhere: the plan tab selector, the generate/regenerate buttons, the empty state, and the ride preference section in Settings. All three labels are consistent across every part of the app.

d: Goals and settings no longer re-ask after sign-in — login now syncs both ways
det: Every sign-in (Google, username/password, PIN unlock, and iOS PWA auto-restore) now runs a load-then-push cycle: it pulls the latest data from Firebase first, then immediately pushes any local data that Firebase is missing back up. This fixes the root cause of goals, activities, and Strava reappearing after reinstall or signing in on a new device — the profile was stored locally but never made it to Firebase because the sync only ran on explicit data changes. Now the first login after any gap automatically closes that gap.

d: Bodyweight exercises added; "Home week" toggle skips the gym without changing your profile
det: 18 new bodyweight exercises added across all session types: push-ups (standard, decline, diamond), pike push-up, inverted row, superman, bodyweight squat, jump squat, bodyweight lunge, single-leg glute bridge, donkey kick, wall sit, mountain climber, bicycle crunch, side plank, floor leg raise, crunch, and burpee. Each has full coaching cues and Traditional Chinese translation. Every slot in every workout type now includes bodyweight alternatives — when gym equipment is unavailable (e.g. home gym profile), the app automatically falls back to bodyweight versions without you having to do anything. The new "Training from home this week?" toggle on the Plan tab forces bodyweight-only session generation for that week only, without permanently changing your gym profile — tap it again or shift to a different week to turn it off. A purple "Home week" badge appears on each gym-day screen so you know the mode is active.

d: "Gym only" replaces "No biking"; plan now respects your training-days-per-week setting
det: The third plan mode was renamed from "No biking" to "Gym only" — a much clearer description of what it actually does. More importantly, the weekly plan generator now honours the training-days-per-week setting from your profile (3–6 days). Previously every mode hard-coded 6 active days regardless of what you set. Now: Gym only = your chosen number of gym days, worst-weather days become rest. With rides = 2 ride days + (target days − 2) gym days + rest. For example, a 4-day user on "Use weather" gets 2 rides + 2 gym + 3 rest instead of 2 rides + 4 gym + 1 rest. The "Gym only" option also now appears in the Ride preference section of Settings so you can switch without going back to the Plan tab. Cycling-specific options (Use weather / Indoor only) are hidden on the Plan tab for users who have no cycling activity selected.

d: Goals, Strava and bike plan now survive reinstalls and sign-outs
det: Profile data (goals, activities, training days, experience level) and the Strava token were never included in the Firebase sync — so reinstalling the app or signing out and back in cleared them, causing the goals onboarding sheet to reappear and Strava to disconnect. All of this data is now included in saveToCloud. The goals and bike plan setup sheets also now push to Firebase immediately on save, so the data is backed up the moment you tap Save rather than waiting for the next log entry.

d: Friendlier ride-log message — explains Strava syncs on its own and may just need time
det: The hint on the manual ride log was reworded. The old wording ("Strava has no ride logged for today") sounded like the ride would never sync. It now makes clear that a connected Strava ride syncs in automatically once Strava finishes processing it — so you can skip the form — and that manual entry is there if you want it tracked right away. For users without Strava, the message is more encouraging about logging to keep progress moving.

d: Ride logging is now inline on the ride card (no pop-up); Weekly Review set to "coming soon"
det: The manual ride log no longer opens a separate screen. The duration, distance, average heart rate, perceived effort and notes fields now sit directly on the ride card and save as you type — with a short note explaining that rides sync automatically once Strava is connected. The Weekly Review email setup in Settings is temporarily shown as "coming soon" while the email backend is being finished; it will be switched back on alongside the Feedback feature.

d: Import now accepts CSV files — restore workouts, rides and PRs from a CSV export
det: The Restore button previously only accepted the JSON backup. It now also reads the CSV produced by Export CSV: it parses workout sets, rides and personal records back into the app, matching exercise names in English or Chinese. CSV import merges into your existing data rather than wiping it, and preserves any fields the CSV does not carry. Rows whose exercise name is not recognised are skipped and reported. The JSON backup is still the recommended full backup (it also carries your plan and settings); CSV import is handy for restoring training records specifically.

d: Performance — weather cached, AI coach recovers from failures, exercise images cached offline
det: Three optimisations. (1) The AI coach previously marked its daily batch as "done" before the network call returned — so a single failed request disabled AI coaching for the rest of the day. It now only marks the batch done after a successful response, with an in-memory guard against duplicate concurrent calls. (2) Weather is cached for 3 hours per week and location, so regenerating your plan no longer re-hits the weather API every time. (3) The service worker now caches exercise demo images from the free-exercise-db CDN — they load instantly on repeat views and work fully offline (previously cross-origin "opaque" responses were skipped by the cache).

d: CSV export, manual ride logging fix, cleaner language labels, and a Feedback section preview
det: Export data now offers a readable CSV (open it in Excel or Sheets to see every workout set, ride and PR as a plain table) alongside the existing JSON backup used for restore. Manual ride logging now appears on any ride day that Strava did not auto-capture — previously it was hidden entirely whenever a Strava account was connected, so connected users could not log a ride Strava missed. The language switcher no longer shows the stray "GB" / "HK" letters (unsupported flag emoji) before English / 繁體中文. A Feedback & Wishlist section was added to Settings as a coming-soon preview.

d: Chinese translation expanded — all 61 exercise names, form cues, coach messages, and the workout day screen
det: All 61 exercises now show proper Traditional Chinese names (硬舉, 深蹲, 臥推, 引體向上, etc.) everywhere they appear — day screen, log, history, PRs and swap sheets. The 💡 form-cue tip on every exercise card is now translated. The "Coach says" pre-workout messages are fully translated for every energy level. The workout day screen UI is now translated too: the Exercises heading, Animate / Tutorial / collapse buttons, Busy? and Log sets buttons, set/rep badges, the back and swap buttons, and the log-workout button.

d: Fixed the Swap Workout sheet showing raw code instead of workout names
det: After workout labels were made translatable (lazy functions), the "Change workout for this day" sheet was still rendering them directly — so it showed text like ()=>_T('wt_push') instead of "Push". The swap sheet now calls the label and description functions correctly, matching every other screen.

d: Chinese language polish — history screen translated, overcrowding fixes, layout class added
det: The Workout History screen is now fully translated (Completed, exercise/set counts, set rows). Added a lang-zh class on the page root when Traditional Chinese is active, with CSS rules that slightly reduce font sizes, allow exercise card titles to wrap to two lines instead of truncating, tighten button padding, and shrink the bottom-nav labels so nothing overflows. The My Training tab label was shortened to 訓練. Language preference now syncs to the cloud, so it restores correctly after signing in on a new device. Exercise-name and coach-message translation are still to come.

d: Weekly AI Review added — a Sunday training analysis covering 8 weeks of data
det: Every Sunday a card appears on the Plan tab offering a weekly review. Tapping Generate sends your last 8 weeks of gym sessions, ride data (Strava or manually logged), all-time PRs and the current plan to the AI coach. It returns four sections: an honest performance summary, progressive overload targets for next week, recovery flags, and one focus goal. The result is cached per week and synced to the cloud, so reopening the app the same Sunday never re-calls the API. An optional "Email me this summary" button delivers it via EmailJS once you add your email and EmailJS keys in Settings. Fully bilingual.

d: Strava sync now pulls 8 weeks of ride history (was 30 days) to power the upcoming weekly AI review
det: The Strava activity sync window was extended from 30 to 56 days, and the page size raised to 100 activities, so the app always holds a full 8 weeks of ride data — distance, duration, average heart rate and average power are all included in each activity. This history feeds the weekly AI review. Existing behaviour (per-day ride matching, plan auto-adapt) is unaffected; it simply has more data to work with.

d: Manual ride logging added for cyclists who haven't connected Strava
det: On any ride day, users without a Strava connection now see a "Log this ride" button. Tapping it opens a form to record duration, distance, average heart rate, perceived effort (RPE) and free-text notes. Logged rides are saved alongside gym sessions, sync to the cloud automatically, and display in a summary card that can be edited later. This ride data also feeds the upcoming weekly AI review. Strava-connected users are unaffected — their rides still pull in automatically. Fully bilingual (English / 繁體中文).

d: Custom PNG icons replace emoji throughout the app — workout types, nav tabs, activities, logo
det: All major emoji icons replaced with purpose-built PNG graphics: each gym workout type (Push/Pull/Legs/Upper Pump) has its own icon, cycling and ride days use a proper bicycle image, rest days show the mobility graphic, activity chips in Settings use the corresponding sport icons, and nav tabs use the branded icon set. The app logo symbol appears in the lock screen and screen headers. Emoji fallbacks activate automatically if an icon fails to load, so the app always looks correct even offline.

d: New users now see a 3-step welcome guide on the Plan tab instead of a blank "no plan" state
det: When someone opens the app for the first time without a profile, the Plan tab now shows a friendly welcome screen with three numbered steps: set up your profile, generate your first plan, and start training. Step 1 is highlighted with a call-to-action button; steps 2 and 3 are greyed out until reached. Once a profile exists, the tab shows the standard "Ready to generate your plan" state with the preference tabs and Generate button.

d: Exercise "Coach" button renamed to "Tips" — more accurate label for hardcoded guidance
det: The Coach button on each exercise opened a hardcoded tips panel with connection cues, setup notes, rep execution and what to avoid — not live AI coaching. Renamed to Tips with a 💡 icon to set the right expectation. The AI Coach section at the top of each workout day is the actual real-time coaching.

d: Traditional Chinese language support added — switch between English and 繁體中文 in Settings
det: Added a full translations system with English and Traditional Chinese. Tap Settings → Language to switch. Translated: navigation tabs, screen subtitles, all section headers, workout type names, day names, energy selector, activity names, and key toasts. The language preference is saved locally and applied instantly on switch.

d: Sign-up hardened — orphaned accounts prevented, password length validated before attempting
det: Fixed a gap where Firebase Auth could create an account but the database write immediately after could fail, leaving a user permanently locked out. Now if the database registration fails after auth creation, the auth account is automatically deleted so the user can try again cleanly. Also added an early password length check (minimum 6 chars) before any network call is made.

d: Active activity chips now have a − button to remove instantly; "Change my activities" button removed
det: Each active activity chip (Cycling, Gym & Weights, etc.) now has a red − button on the right to remove it directly. The redundant "Change my activities" button is gone — add and remove are now handled entirely from the chips. The "Set up activities" button only appears when you have no activities at all.

d: Every changelog entry now has expandable detail explaining the logic and reasoning behind the change
det: Tap any version row in What's New to expand a longer explanation of why the change was made, how the logic works, and any relevant context. Useful for understanding what the app actually does under the hood or checking if a specific behaviour was intentional.

d: Tapping + Add on an activity now adds it instantly — no more going through the full setup screen
det: Each activity chip has its own + Add button. Tapping it immediately writes that activity into your profile and confirms with a green toast. Previously all chips opened the full goals setup screen, which was unnecessary when you just wanted to add one thing. The ⓘ button still opens the info popup independently.

d: Skipping a gym day automatically shifts the rest of the week — no prompts, no dropped muscle groups
det: When you swap a gym day to Rest, the app finds all remaining gym days that week and cascades the missed workout type through them in order — Push moves to the next gym slot, that slot's type moves to the one after it, and so on. Cycling, running, cardio, and rest days are completely ignored by the cascade; only Push/Pull/Legs/Upper Pump sessions shift.

d: Activity chips now show an ⓘ info button explaining what each activity covers; renamed to Cardio & Classes
det: Added a small ⓘ button to the right of every activity chip (both active and the dashed + Add ones). Tapping it opens a sheet describing what that activity covers in the app and what syncs automatically. Also renamed the fourth activity from "Other Cardio" to "Cardio & Classes" to better reflect that it covers HIIT, rowing, elliptical, stair master, swimming, group fitness and similar.
